# School of Engineering

Discover your future at the School of Engineering.

Last updated 27 August 2025

**Discover your future at the School of Engineering**

Are you interested in using engineering to create innovative solutions for a better environment? Offering relevant programmes that teach you essential concepts and technical skills, you will learn how to apply your knowledge creatively to improve how we work, live, and play.**Gain skills for a successful career in engineering**

At this school, you will train in a real-world environment that encourages creativity and an entrepreneurial spirit. Our programmes help you develop not only technical skills but also important values that will support your career success. By gaining a mix of technological, methodological, and social competencies, you will be well-prepared to adapt to the ever-changing global economy.

## Experience cutting-edge technology at the Autobotics Centre

### (Technology Blk, Level 1)

Welcome to the Autobotics Centre, where you will explore the exciting world of industrial automation and robotics. This hands-on facility is designed to give you practical training in automation and robotic applications, while encouraging your involvement in real-world projects. Here, you will learn how to operate Industry 4.0 systems and work with collaborative robots that are shaping the future of manufacturing.

### Build essential skills for tomorrow's industries

At the Centre, both students and staff develop valuable competencies in the latest Industry 4.0 technologies where you will gain the technical skills needed to succeed in a rapidly changing environment. This unique learning experience prepares you for a successful career in the growing fields of automation and robotics.

## Shape the future of smart buildings at the Centre for Built Environment

### (Technology Blk, Level 3)

The Centre for Built Environment offers comprehensive training on modern building systems and their integration for smarter energy use. This centre focuses on teaching you how to create intelligent control systems that improve efficiency in buildings. Here, you will gain hands-on experience that prepares you for a successful career in the built environment sector.

### Develop practical skills in building systems

At the Centre for Built Environment, you will learn how to install, operate, troubleshoot, and service various building equipment and controls. This includes working with systems such as chilled water, fire detection, and swimming pool management. You will also discover how to connect these systems with Building Management System software, equipping you with the skills needed to excel in this growing field.

## Discover the ITE-Johnson Controls Centre for smart living

### (Technology Blk, Level 1)

The ITE-Johnson Controls Building Technologies & Solutions Centre equips you with essential skills for managing smart living environments. As buildings become increasingly digital, this centre prepares you to work with modern systems and solutions. You will also focus on promoting smart and sustainable facilities management, setting you up for a successful career in this exciting field.

### Enhance your learning in an innovative environment

The ITE-Johnson Controls Centre serves as a creative space for educators to develop new teaching methods and innovative ways are to engage students in their learning. This collaborative atmosphere ensures that you receive a high-quality education that aligns with the latest industry trends and demands.

## Inspire your green thumb at our exciting Landscape Courtyard

### (Business Blk, Lower Ground)

The Landscape Courtyard is a vibrant training space designed to give you real-world experience in horticulture. This facility features four interactive zones, including the Landscape Courtyard, Urban Greenery Hub, Hort Hub, and Nursery, where you can engage in activities like terrarium care and tree climbing. With a stunning 5m green wall and a 3m high waterfall, learning about plants and landscapes at ITE is both fun and inspiring!

### Explore innovative techniques in urban greenery management

Here, you will discover the latest technology in Urban Greenery Management. The Gallery showcases exciting tools like drones and sonic tomographs, which you will use to assess trees and learn about modern practices. Comfortable, air-conditioned classrooms are connected to the outdoor areas, allowing you to learn important theories and apply them right away in a practical setting.

## Experience real-world learning at the Plant for Authentic Learning

### (Technology Blk, Level 2)

The Plant for Authentic Learning offers you the chance to gain practical experience in chemical processes. This workshop features scaled-down process pilot plants that mimic those used in the petrochemical and pharmaceutical industries. Here, you will receive hands-on training in operating and controlling continuous processes, preparing you for a successful career in manufacturing.

### Develop essential skills for the chemical industry

In this workshop, you will learn the important skills needed to work in modern chemical manufacturing facilities. The hands-on training allows you to understand how these processes operate in real-world settings. By participating in this dynamic learning environment, you will be well-equipped for future opportunities in the petrochemical and pharmaceutical sectors.

## Elevate your skills at the Vertical Transportation Laboratory

### (Business Blk, Level 5)

The Lab offers a comprehensive training environment focused on lift and escalator systems. Inside the laboratory, you will find a 6-storey lift simulator that helps you understand how a lift system operates in detail. This engaging setup prepares you for hands-on learning with actual lift and escalator systems located in the outdoor laboratory.

### Gain essential skills in vertical transportation systems

In this lab, you will develop the skills needed to work with modern vertical transportation systems. The combination of simulated and real-world training ensures you gain valuable experience that is relevant to the industry. By participating in this dynamic learning environment, you will be well-prepared for a successful career in the field of vertical transportation.

# Other facilities

Check out our student-related, general and retail facilities at ITE College East.

Last updated 27 August 2025

## Education & Career Centre

### (Administration Blk, Level 1)

**Opening hours: Mon - Fri, 8.30am to 5.30pm****Email:** [**ce_career_services_centre@ite.edu.sg**](mailto:ce_career_services_centre@ite.edu.sg)

The Education & Career Centre is a one-stop centre providing a range of Education and Career Coaching (ECC) services to assist and support students and graduates making well-informed decisions about their academic progression, training and career choices.Make an  [appointment with our Education & Career Coaches now](/about-ite/colleges/college-east/facilities/ecc-appointment-booking/) .

## Performing Arts Centre - PAC

### (Administration Blk, Level 2)

The Centre houses two dance studios with full-length mirrors, 2 sound proof orchestra rooms, a rehearsal studio, an art studio and a soundproof jamming studio. Access to the facilities is by booking with the Centre’s office during operating hours. The Performing Arts Centre is set up to expose students in the appreciation of art forms, be it in dance, music, drama, literature or the fine arts.

Through the Centre’s activities, the students will be exposed to different art forms to stimulate their interests and uncover latent talents. Each year, talented ITE students are scouted from among the Colleges’ Music and Arts clubs and invited to join the Performing Arts Centre. As a performing artiste with the Performing Arts Centre, students will have the opportunity to realise their fullest potential under the guidance of trained professionals.

## Sports facilities

The campus is equipped with a wide range of sports facilities to promote healthy lifestyles. Students can utilise the indoor and outdoor facilities, as part of their co-curricular activities, or during their leisure hours.

Indoor sports facilities
- The Gymnasium (Business Block, Level 1) is well-equipped with cardiovascular, strength training equipment and a free-weight training area.
- The Indoor Sports Hall (ISH, Business Block, Level 3) has 8 badminton courts, a basketball court/floorball court/handball court (shared), a volleyball court and 4 sepak takraw courts
- The Dance Studio (Business Block, Level 5 – within MPSH) is encased with full length mirrors and fitted with a LED TV and DVD playerOutdoor sports facilities
- A Sports Stadium with a 4-lane running track and sports field with seating capacity of 823 spectators
- A 9-lane Olympic-sized Swimming Pool with seating capacity of 270 spectators at the gallery
- The Multi-Purpose Court has 2 basketball courts, 2 sepak takraw courts, 2 volleyball courts and a netball court
- 3 Street Soccer Courts
- 1 Tennis Court
- A 10m x 9m Rock Climbing Wall for beginner, intermediate and advanced climbers
- A Bouldering Wall located along Level 1 of Business Blk

## Student Activity Centre - SAC

### (Business Blk, Level 2)

**Opening hours: Mon - Fri, 8.30am to 6.00pm**

The SAC is located at Business Block, Level 2. The Centre houses special rooms for clubs and interest groups. It is a place where students with similar hobbies and interests can gather and socialise. This facility also houses the Student Council Office.

## Counselling @ Student Care

### (Administration Blk, Level 2)

**Opening hours: Mon – Fri, 8.30am to 5.30pm****Email:** [**dear_ce_counsellor@ite.edu.sg**](mailto:dear_ce_counsellor@ite.edu.sg)

Need to talk? The life of a student can sometimes be overwhelming and is often a challenge. If you are feeling down or concerned about something, come and talk with us. Our friendly counsellors are more than glad to discuss your issues with you and support you with your personal and emotional challenges.  Rest assure that you will be treated with care, privacy and respect.

# About College West

Welcome to ITE College West!

Last updated 29 June 2026

ITE College West (CW) is home to more than 8,000 full-time and 5,000 part-time students, and about 700 academic and administrative staff. Our campus is located in Choa Chu Kang.

We set our focus to be a “College of Service and Innovation” and currently, offer courses through the Schools of:

- Business & Services
- Electronics & Info-Comm Technology
- Engineering
- Hospitality

There are several cutting edge training facilities in our College such as Hotel West (functional 14-room hotel), Amber West (student-operated fine-dining restaurant), Urban Mobility Centre, Drone & Robot Hub, and VIBES Retail Zone.

CW is also a vibrant campus that offers more than 80 CCAs for students to pick from.

Follow us on social media:

- [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/itecollegewest/?hl=en)
- [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/itecollegewest/)

# HEARTS IN MOTION

President's Challenge 2026

Last updated 8 July 2026

President's Challenge 2026 Registration Update

| 🚨Registration is Now Closed!We are thrilled to announce that we have officially reached our participant capacity.Thank you to everyone who registered. Your incredible support directly contributes to the President's Challenge 2026 and helps make a meaningful difference.We look forward to seeing all participants at the starting line on25 July 2026!💝 Missed Out on Registration?You can still support our cause by making a direct donation. Every contribution big or small, helps us create a greater impact and support those in need.👉 Donate here:https://giving.sg/donate/campaign/hearts-in-motion |
| --- |

## About the Event

***Hearts in Motion***brings individuals, communities and families together in support of the President’s Challenge 2026 - uplifting aspirations and lives of those facing challenges.

Designed to be fun, inclusive and accessible, this event aims to:

- Rally community participation through inclusive and accessible activities in support of the President's Challenge
- Promote active living and preventive health across age groups
- Foster community bonding through inclusive multi-generational activities

**Event Details**

**Date**: 25 July 2026

**Time**: 8.00am – 12.00pm

**Venue**: Jurong Lake Gardens, Wave Plaza

**Event Categories**

Choose how you wish to take part:

🏃‍♂️ **5-km Competitive Run**

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 **3-km Family × Team Walk**

**Event Highlights**

Beyond the run and walk, enjoy a vibrant, family-friendly eventwith activities for everyone. These activities create a lively community space where families can connect, play, and build lasting bonds — all while giving back.

🤖 Interactive robotic games

🎯 Fun challenges for children

❤️ Health and fitness assessments

⚽ Sports try-outs

🧸 Plushie booths

🍰 Homemade food and drinks

**Who Can Join**

We welcome participants from all walks of life. To ensure smooth and enjoyable experience:

- Places are **limited to 1,000 participants**per category
- Registration is on a **first-come, first-served basis**

✨ **Early registration is encouraged** to secure your preferred category.

### Prizes for the 5-km Competitive Run

Top 5 winners of the Open & Veteran categories for the 5-km (Men) & 5-km (Women) will receive the following prizes:

- 1st place - Medal & 1 pair of Brooks Hyperion Elite 5 shoes (retail $398)

- 2nd place - Medal & 1 pair of Brooks Hyperion Max 3 shoes (retail $268)

- 3rd place - Medal & 1 pair of Brooks Hyperion 3 shoes (retail $208)

- 4th place - Medal & $100 Brooks voucher & 1 pair of Brooks socks

- 5th place - Medal & $60 Brooks voucher & 1 pair of Brooks socks

### Race & Walk Entitlement

**5‑km Competitive Run:**Participants will receive a race pack, which includes the official event T‑shirt.

**3‑km Family x Team Walk:**Each group member in the Family x Team walk will receive one goodie bag. There will be no event T‑shirts provided for this category. Families and teams are encouraged to come in your own themed T‑shirts, with a splash of red.

# School of Hospitality

The School of Hospitality (SOH) offers various hospitality-related courses at the Technical Diploma and Higher Nitec levels to support the fields of Culinary Arts, Pastry and Baking, and Hospitality Operations.

Last updated 1 September 2025

Singapore's status as a top leisure and business destination is globally acknowledged, fuelling the growing demand for chefs, service personnel and Food & Beverage staff. Aptly so, the School of Hospitality (SOH) plays a pivotal role as the industry copes with ever increasing expectations.

SOH is College West's niche school. It offers various hospitality-related courses at the Technical Diploma and *Higher Nitec* levels to support the fields of Culinary Arts, Pastry and Baking, and Hospitality Operations.

SOH is also well-placed to produce skilled graduates who would be first-choice employees in the hospitality industry. Take a look at our facilities below for a more authentic impression!

## Crema West & Barista Training Centre (Blk 3 Level 4)

Crema West is a lively F&B space open to the public, staff and students. The service area is managed by students from the Higher Nitec in Hospitality Operations while the kitchen area is supported by students from the Higher Nitec in Culinary Arts and Higher Nitec in Pastry & Baking programmes. Crema West collaborates with industry leaders like Starbucks, Far East Hospitality, Bettr Barista and F&N Singapore. It also hosts team building events for local schools, with activities centered around coffee.

At Crema West, students immerse themselves in a learning environment to perfect their barista craft and explore the intricacies of running a café. They learn to select and grind coffee beans, prepare different types of coffee and hot beverages and keep the barista station clean and organised. They also handle various aspects of F&B operations, like cashiering and displaying merchandise for sale.

Facility-supported courses:

- *Higher Nitec* in Culinary Arts
- *Higher Nitec* in Hospitality Operations
- *Higher Nitec* in Pastry & Baking

## Hotel West (Blk 2 Level 7)

Hotel West is a nature-inspired training hotel with 14 rooms, including 1 Junior suite and 13 Deluxe rooms, for guests to book and stay in style. Guests get to enjoy warm reception services and unwind in the executive lounge and sky lobby.

At Hotel West, students are trained to identify ways to improve sustainability and care economy practices, and create communication materials for stakeholders. With exposure in handling guest services at the front desk, they learn to build strong relationships with guests and manage their expectations while ensuring smooth and efficient operations.

Facility-supported course:

- *Higher Nitec* in Hospitality Operations

## Training Kitchens

### Hybrid Training Kitchen (Blk 2 Level 3)

Experience versatile learning in the Hybrid Training Kitchen where classroom and kitchen practical lessons are made possible with configurable furniture. Through collaborative initiatives with BreadTalk, students benefit from engaging visits by professional bakers and learning journeys.

In the Training Kitchen, students unleash their creativity as they conduct product research and development, nutrition and sensory analysis to design new menus and create customised baking products.

Facility-supported course:

- *Higher Nitec* in Pastry & Baking

### La Vie (Blk 2 Level 4) and La Gloire (Blk 2 Level 3)

La Vie and La Gloire are fully equipped kitchens featuring workstations with burners, ovens, under-counter chillers, combi-ovens and salamanders, providing students with a comprehensive culinary learning experience. These kitchens have hosted partnerships with numerous industry leaders, including US Poultry and Bocuse d'Or Academy Singapore.

In the training kitchens, students learn to use advanced cooking techniques to create dishes tailored to consumers' tastes. They gain skills to identify business opportunities in the hospitality sector, craft innovative solutions and use marketing strategies to develop business plans.

Facility-supported courses:

- *Higher Nitec* in Culinary Arts
- Technical Diploma in Culinary Arts with Restaurant Management

### Patisserie (Blk 2 Level 4)

Patisserie Training Kitchen is equipped with state-of-the-art equipment, including industry-standard pastry ovens, blast chillers and mixers to meet various training needs. It features collaborative workstations that encourage teamwork and peer learning to simulate real-world kitchen environments. Students also have access to specialised tools like piping bags, specialty moulds, sugarcraft tools and chocolate tempering tools. The training kitchen has hosted the Vietnamese team for Food Hotel Asia 2024 for their pastry competition preparation.

Here, students master the techniques of pastry-making, as well as evaluate and store pastry fillings. They design cakes and perform decorative work. Additionally, students learn the art of crafting menus for pastry and dessert products and plan promotional strategies to market them.

Facility-supported course:

- *Higher Nitec* in Pastry & Baking

## Training Restaurants

### Amber West (Blk 2 Level 4)

Amber West offers an authentic environment where students experience the day-to-day running of a restaurant for both lunch and dinner services, preparing them for the realities of working in the F&B industry. It features a seating capacity for 60 diners, along with a private dining room available upon special request.

At Amber West, students take on different roles within F&B outlets, performing tasks such as preparing the restaurant for service, conducting roll calls and hosting guests. They also develop a solid understanding of the service industry and learn about the expectations for service excellence.

Facility-supported courses:

- *Higher Nitec* in Culinary Arts
- *Higher Nitec* in Hospitality Operations
- *Higher Nitec* in Pastry & Baking

### Chez West (Blk 2 Level 3)

Partnered with the prestigious French culinary school, Institut Lyfe, Chez West offers a rich learning experience for students to gain valuable knowledge in the art of French cooking.

Students learn to apply advanced cooking techniques and work on various themes to create dishes on offer in a gastronomic restaurant. They also develop wine tasting skills to identify flavours, create wine lists and recommend pairings with dishes. Additionally, students get hands-on experience by setting up a restaurant and learning how to run a kitchen smoothly.

Facility-supported course:

- Technical Diploma in Culinary Arts with Restaurant Management

### Topaz West (Blk 2 Level 4)

The setup at Topaz West is highly versatile, allowing it to transform into a fine dining restaurant for events or be used as an academic facility for lessons. It serves multiple purposes, including competition training, hosting dinners and parent-teacher meetings and providing ad hoc dining etiquette workshops for MOE partners.

At Topaz, students learn the basics of Restaurant Service, Beverage Service and Tableside Service.

Facility-supported course:

- *Higher Nitec* in Hospitality Operations

## Vine West (Blk 2 Level 1)

Vines West provides students with a genuine venue for both practical and theoretical lessons in wine and beverage training. It includes a full bar setup for making alcoholic cocktails and non-alcoholic mocktails, along with a Practice Bar station for students to refine their bar skills and undergo assessments. The facility also features a table and seating area for practising wine service.

Students learn to prepare and serve a variety of alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages, including mocktails, cocktails and wines.

Facility-supported course:

- *Higher Nitec* in Hospitality Operations

# School of Business & Services

The School of Business & Services (SBS) also offers our students a conducive and authentic learning environment that encourages entrepreneurship, teamwork and creativity.

Last updated 29 June 2026

The School of Business & Services (SBS) at CW is home to some of the most passionate teaching staff in ITE. Our lecturers deliver innovative training and quality education to produce enterprising and employable graduates.

SBS also offers our students a conducive and authentic learning environment that encourages entrepreneurship, teamwork and creativity. The School consistently receives top billings for its programmes, student feedback and successful alumni.

We produce resourceful and intelligent young adult learners, who will continue to make a difference in the world.

## Customer Engagement Lab (Blk 4 Level 4)

Customer Engagement Lab simulates a lively customer experience centre where students participate in realistic scenarios that reflect real-world customer interactions. This hands-on practice helps them to sharpen their problem-solving, communication and multitasking skills.

Students learn to evaluate service experience and quality, perform data analytics, and redesign services and operations.

Facility-supported courses:

- *Higher Nitec* in Customer Experience
- *Higher Nitec* in Service Management

## PULSE (Blk 2 Level 2)

PULSE is an innovative hub dedicated to shaping the future of healthcare service professionals. The hub prepares students with the skills needed to excel in the healthcare industry. At PULSE, students learn to manage communication with patients, perform analytics for healthcare institutions, and implement infection prevention and control measures.

Facility-supported course:

- Work-Study Diploma in Patient Management & Services

## Spark Wellness Hub (Blk 4 Level 4)

Spark Fitness Hub is designed to meet the latest fitness industry needs using industry-standard equipment and protocols. Here, students can use modern technology, analytical sensors and rehabilitative machinery to enhance their sports management learning journey.

At the Hub, students perform fitness testing and design fitness programmes. They learn to implement sport safety measures and management strategies. Additionally, students handle routine finance and general administration tasks for managing sports activities.

Facility-supported courses:

- *Higher Nitec* in Sport Management
- Technical Diploma in Health & Exercise Coaching
- Work-Study Diploma in Fitness Management

## VIBES Retail Zone (Blk 2 Level 2)

Partnered with industry leaders like Decks and LUXASIA, VIBES Retail Zone is a modern space furnished with the latest retail features like live streaming, smart technology, perfumery training and predictive AI. It offers a cutting-edge environment for students to engage with the newest trends in retail industry.

There are three distinct areas in VIBES —APEX, B.BOX, and CHIC, where students learn various retail practices and skills. Students will learn how to promote products and services through face-to-face interactions, online platforms and live streaming. They will also explore predictive analytics, which helps businesses understand customer behaviour and make informed decisions. Additionally, they will discover how to implement sustainability measures on retail practices that are environmentally friendly.

Facility-supported course:

- *Higher Nitec* in Retail & Online Business

# School of Electronics & Info-Comm Technology

From artificial intelligence to data engineering, internet of things to info-comm technology, the School of Electronics & Info-Comm Technology provides our students with real-world skills and experience to solve real-world problems.

Last updated 27 August 2025

The fields of Electronics and Info-Comm Technology are a potent combination that is revolutionising the world over today. Towards this end, the courses offered by our School of Electronics and Info-Comm Technology (SEIT) are always enriching, dynamic and relevant.

From artificial intelligence to data engineering, internet of things to info-comm technology, the School provides our students with real-world skills and experience to solve real-world problems. As we continue to move with times, courses offered by SEIT will always lead to exciting careers.

If you aspire to be among those in the high-growth electronics and info-comm technology sectors, this School is the one for you!

## AIoT & Automation Lab (Blk 4 Level 6)

AIoT & Automation Lab showcases systems and equipment focused on Artificial Intelligence, the Internet of Things and Automation & Autonomous Systems. In collaboration with Bosch Rexroth, the Lab provides students with access to the latest tools and knowledge, making their learning experience exciting and relevant.

Students will gain skills, knowledge and professional qualities to integrate, deploy and manage systems using advanced manufacturing technologies.

Facility-supported course:

- Work-Study Diploma in Electronics & Computer Engineering (Applied Electronics & AI)

## Data Experience Lab (Blk 5 Level 3)

Data Experience Lab is where students explore the world of data with a real plant wall. Here, students use sensors to collect, clean and analyse data. They create data visualisations to gain insights and manage databases effectively. The Lab also provides students with valuable exposure to Google solutions for data science projects and tasks.

Facility-supported course:

- *Higher Nitec* in Data Engineering

## Drone & Robot Hub (Blk 1 Level 4)

The Drone & Robot Hub features an 8K-resolution LED video wall offering a 180-degree viewing experience, alongside advanced robots and drones. The hub is setup in collaboration with industry giants like Aruba, AWS, DJI, HP, Intel, UBTECH, Slamtec, Softbank and Weston Robot. These partnerships provide access to the latest technologies and expertise, enriching the learning experience for the students and ensuring the curriculum stays aligned with industry trends.

At the Hub, students improve their Python programming skills by working with drones, humanoid and wheeled robots. They gain practical experience in robot programming, sensor integration, navigation and control, which are essential skills for the future of robotics.

Facility-supported courses:

- *Higher Nitec* in AI Applications
- *Higher Nitec* in Cyber & Network Security
- *Higher Nitec* in Data Engineering
- *Higher Nitec* in Electronics Engineering
- *Higher Nitec* in IT Applications Development
- *Higher Nitec* in IT Systems & Networks
- *Higher Nitec* in Security System Integration

## Mobile Apps Lab (Blk 4 Level 3)

Mobile Apps Lab is inspired by a minimalist start-up aesthetic, highlighted with vibrant colours. The modern and immersive layout creates a stylish environment where students can learn and develop mobile applications. With tools and support from Adobe, students have everything they need to bring their app ideas to life.

Students learn to design UI/UX, develop and support web and mobile applications, create and maintain content and perform software testing.

Facility-supported course:

- *Higher Nitec*in IT Applications Development

## System Integration Lab (Blk 3 Level 4)

System Integration Lab offers a state-of-the-art learning space with cutting-edge technology. From Smart Lighting to Facial Recognition access, wireless ceiling microphone systems to Wi-Fi 6 with access control and a writable magic glass wall, all made possible through a partnership with HPE Aruba Networks.

In this Lab, students learn to manage cloud platforms, enterprise networks and system infrastructure. They transform data into valuable information and create visual elements to support business decisions. By applying AI technology, students assess and enhance network performance, preparing themselves for careers as Associate Infrastructure Support Engineers in the IT industry.

Facility-supported courses:

- *Higher Nitec* in IT Systems & Networks
- Work-Study Diploma in IT System Integration

# School of Engineering

College West's School of Engineering is dedicated to providing a dynamic and cutting-edge education that prepares our students for success in the rapidly changing world of technical landscape.

Last updated 1 September 2025

College West's School of Engineering is dedicated to providing a dynamic and cutting-edge education that prepares our students for success in the rapidly changing world of technical landscape. Our industry-savvy faculties prepare our graduates to be well-versed in current technologies and well-equipped to navigate and contribute to the dynamic field of engineering and technology.

If it’s engineering, it rocks!

## Automation & Robotics Centre (Blk 1 Level 4)

Automation & Robotics Centre is a dynamic place for students to learn about the Advanced Manufacturing Industry. The centre provides a modern learning environment with a training system where students explore key concepts like Industry 4.0, digitalisation and the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT).

Students gain experiential learning in Manufacturing Execution Systems, Radio Frequency Identification and Augmented Reality. They work with digital twins for real-time analysis, allowing them to programme and test "what-if" scenarios, even with limited physical machines or during remote learning. Students also learn to programme and operate next-generation robots and explore IIoT technologies such as Ethernet/IP and IO-Link protocols.

Facility-supported courses:

- *Nitec*in Mechatronics and Robotics
- *Higher Nitec* in Mechatronics Engineering
- Work-Study Diploma in Port Automation Technology

## Built Environment Hub (Blk 6 Level 6)

Built Environment Hub is an integrated space where students can monitor key facility systems in real-time. The setup is supported by industry partners like Daikin Airconditioning and C&W Services, who offer their valuable resources and expertise. The hub features a fully operational bathroom model for learning installation and maintenance, and a mobile display generator for understanding electrical components. It is also equipped with an exploded view of a cassette air-con fan coil unit and a sprinkler testing room to enhance learning experience.

Students learn to maintain mechanical and electrical systems, along with air-conditioning and ventilation systems. They are taught to oversee the Green Building Management System and ensure good housekeeping and Workplace Safety & Health practices at the work sites.

Facility-supported courses:

- *Higher Nitec* in Facilities Management & Engineering
- Work-Study Diploma in Facilities Management

## Bus Engineering Lab (Blk 5 Level 1)

Bus Engineering Lab features an e-bus chassis, electrical axle, electronic destination system, electrical bus door training system, bus air conditioning system and a decommissioned double-decker bus. With equipment donated by ITE partners such as the ZF, SBST, EDS and BYD, students benefit from hands-on training with both combustion engine and electric bus technologies.

In the Lab, students gain practical skills to assemble and diagnose faults in bus systems, as well as fix high voltage electric circuits. They also work with basic electro-pneumatics and electro-hydraulic circuits used in buses and heavy vehicles.

Facility-supported courses:

- *Nitec*in Automotive Technology
- *Higher Nitec* in Automotive Engineering
- Technical Engineer Diploma in Automotive Engineering
- Work-Study Diploma in Land Transport Engineering (Vehicle)

## Clean Energy Lab (Blk 6 Level 4)

Clean Energy Lab offers a grid-tie demonstration that shows how solar photovoltaic systems are connected to the electrical grid. Equipped with industry-standard equipment, the Lab features a buoyant platform system that supports and maintains solar panels on the water's surface. The setup is supported by the partnership with Sembcorp Industries.

Students explore the world of solar power through hands-on training by designing efficient layouts, installing components and maintaining photovoltaic arrays for optimal energy generation. They also implement cutting-edge technologies and strategies to create sustainable systems with smart automation, security and environmental controls.

Facility-supported course:

- *Higher Nitec* in Electrical Engineering

## Lighting & Sound Experiential Lab (Blk 6 Level 4)

Lighting & Sound Experiential Lab features impressive LED walls that showcase large digital displays with vibrant full-colour graphics. The learning environment is enhanced by collaborations with industry leaders like Sennheiser and ROBE Lighting. This allows students to experiment with different lighting and sound techniques and learn how to design stunning visual displays and powerful audio setups.

In this space, students create visual effects presentations using projection mapping with customised graphics. Students also learn to operate and maintain advanced sound mixing consoles and set up stage lighting and LED walls for events.

Facility-supported course:

- *Higher Nitec* in Electrical Engineering

## Plant Equipment Maintenance Lab (Blk 5 Level 2)

Plant Equipment Maintenance Lab provides authentic training using a variety of pumps, valves, hand tools, and pipe bending and fabrication tools. This setup ensures that students gain meaningful real-world experience, equipping them to confidently tackle complex challenges in their future careers.

Students learn to install, service, troubleshoot, and repair machinery, pumping systems, and pneumatic and hydraulic systems. They also gain skills in fabricating and reconditioning machine parts using basic hand tools, power tools and drilling machines, as well as rectifying electrical faults in machinery.

Facility-supported courses:

- *Nitec*in Mechanical Technology
- Work-Study Diploma in Mechanical Systems Engineering

## Rail Engineering Hub (Blk 6 Level 2)

Rail Engineering Hub features key elements such as a de-commissioned train cabin, a bogie assembly, and an overhead catenary system, generously donated by the LTA, SBST and SMRT. This invaluable support from industry partners help enrich the learning environment and give students access to real-world tools and experiences.

Students master essential skills and gain knowledge in areas like rapid transit systems and operations, automation and control systems, and electronics systems and equipment.

Facility-supported courses:

- *Nitec*in Rapid Transit Technology
- *Higher Nitec* in Rapid Transit Engineering
- Work-Study Diploma in Land Transport Engineering (Rail)

## Urban Mobility Centre (Blk 3 Level 1)

The Urban Mobility Centre houses an Automotive Diagnostic Lab that uses smart technology, including wireless diagnostic equipment and realistic simulators. The Electrification and Diagnostic Labs specialise in training students on electric vehicles, focusing on diagnostics and safety for high-voltage systems. This is enhanced by the provision of training cars from partners such as the Hyundai Motor Group Innovation Centre, Singapore.

Students learn to troubleshoot, service, maintain and repair commercial vehicles, passenger vehicles and electric vehicles, including their propulsion systems.

Facility-supported courses:

- *Nitec*in Automotive Technology
- *Higher Nitec* in Automotive Engineering
- Technical Engineer Diploma in Automotive Engineering
- Work-Study Diploma in Land Transport Engineering (Vehicle)

# Other facilities

Check out our student-related, general and retail facilities at ITE College West.

Last updated 27 August 2025

## Experience ITE Centre (Blk 1 Level 4)

The Experience ITE Centre (EIC) is where secondary school students gain insights into what ITE College West has to offer. Whether you are interested in business, engineering, hospitality or IT technology, EIC offers a hub of interactive activities that provide a sneak peek into the diverse courses available.

Both our hallmark 'Experience ITE Programme' and 'Come Visit ITE College West' Programme are tailored to help secondary school students make informed decisions about their educational journey in ITE. During these sessions, secondary school students have the opportunity to interact with knowledgeable ITE educators to better understand the learning environments.

## Sports Complex

The Sports Complex offers an Olympic-size sports arena that supports the teaching of Sports & Wellness modules and a range of sports co-curricular activities. Students are given opportunities to develop their passion for sports such as soccer, rugby, ultimate frisbee and softball, and gain essential skills like teamwork and discipline.

Next to the football stadium are basketball, netball, tennis and futsal courts with a combined seating capacity for up to 800 people. Students can also use these facilities to play sepak takraw, volleyball, handball and practice archery.

## Student Activity Centre (Blk 3 Level 3)

The lively Student Activity Centre (SAC) has a mix of energetic activity zones and quiet corners for students to relax and connect with their peers.

There are two main areas in the SAC - the Activity Zone and the Playzone. In the Activity Zone, there are modular seats that can be rearranged for project discussions. This space also offers fun games like foosball and pool. The Playzone area offers a variety of gaming stations, including PS4, Xbox, Switch and Kinect, for students to have fun playing their favourite games with their friends.

## Student Care Centre (Blk 3 Level 6)

The Student Care Centre (SCC) is your go-to place for support and well-being. SCC provides a safe and cozy space for students to share their thoughts and seek help from our caring counsellors and learning accessibility officers.

Whether you need a listening ear or face challenges due to disabilities or special educational needs, the counselling team and the learning accessibility team are here to support you at ITE College West.

## Student Gym (Blk 6 Level 2)

The Student Gym is where students can elevate their fitness levels through various fitness and conditioning activities structured for Sports & Wellness modules and Sports & Games CCAs.

The gym is well-equipped with a diverse range of strength-training equipment such as stack-weight machines, plate-loaded machines, free weights, kettlebells and cardio machines to suit various training needs and fitness levels. There is also a dance studio within for students to participate in "Look Good Feel Good" group exercise programmes like Bike spinning,, K-Pop, Pilates, Yoga and Zumba.

## Student Services Centre (Blk 3 Level 2)

The Student Services Centre is a one-stop service centre that provides seamless support to students on their administration and financial assistance needs.

From enquiries about fees and financial assistance to insurance claims, student passes and student lockers, our friendly student services team is always ready to help you navigate student life with ease.

## Amber West

Experience a whole new level of dining pleasures away from the hustle and bustle of city life. Boasting a seating capacity for 60 diners, Amber West – a student operated restaurant – offers affordable gourmet selections prepared by student chefs and served by student servers. This fine dining restaurant serves to train students in an authentic learning environment and it features a tantalising collection of Western and Asian cuisines with twists.

To avoid disappointment, we encourage our guests to make online reservations through  [Chope.com](https://cho.pe/dineatamberwestitesg) , for up to 8 people. If you are planning for a larger party, kindly send us an email to  [SOHOutlets@ite.edu.sg](mailto:SOHOutlets@ite.edu.sg)  and we will be happy to organize a memorable meal for you.

## Document: https://www.ite.edu.sg/about-ite/careers-at-ite/benefits-and-engagement/
**Source URL:** https://www.ite.edu.sg/about-ite/careers-at-ite/benefits-and-engagement/

1. [Home](/)
2. [About ITE](/about-ite/)
3. [Careers@ITE](/about-ite/careers-at-ite/)
4. Benefits & Engagement

# Benefits & Engagement

ITE’s suite of comprehensive employee benefits, broadly aligned to the benefits in the Public Service, aims to promote work-life integration and encourage healthy lifestyle

Last updated 14 April 2026

- You will enjoy a wide range of leave benefits which includes vacation, medical, marriage, maternity/paternity, childcare, examination, volunteer and parent-care leave
- You will also receive subsidies for your outpatient medical and dental expenses. We will make additional contributions into your Central Provident Fund Medisave Account for the purchase of hospitalisation insurance for yourself and/or your dependents
- Besides leave and medical/dental benefits, ITE also provides a Flexible Benefit to meet your health and lifestyle needs

You will enjoy free membership with Club ITE, which organises a wide range of social and recreational activities to promote staff well-being and bonding. We have an extensive range of health and sport facilities, and we encourage staff to keep fit and maintain a healthy lifestyle by forming Fitness Teams (FiTs).

As a public officer in ITE, you will also get to:

- [Sign up as a Civil Service Club member](https://www.csc.sg/About-CSC-Membership)  at a nominal fee to enjoy the Civil Service Club chalets at Changi and Loyang at affordable rates, and other member benefits
- Join the Public Officers Group Insurance Scheme which provides coverage against death and permanent disablement for you and your family at low premium rates

# Professional Development Schemes

ITE Academy was set up to formulate, implement and review staff training policies, strategies, schemes and programmes for all ITE staff in line with our National, Industry, Public Service and Education agenda and transformation.

Last updated 27 August 2025

- It promotes comprehensive planning of all learning and development (L&D) activities for all staff groups, with focused attention on staff’s skills relevance, renewal and refresh.
- Develop, coordinate and implement organisation’s total learning plan, training budget and staff professional development schemes
- Four key integrated and holistic approach for staff development

1. Leadership Development
2. Technical & Professional Education and Training (TPET) Capability Development
3. Professional Development
4. Organisational Learning

1. [Home](/)
2. [About ITE](/about-ite/)
3. Be a donor

# Be a donor

Donate to the ITE Education Fund and make a difference.

Last updated 22 December 2025

**Your gift is much needed to support our students’ daily expenses**

ITE has a large enrolment of around 27,000 students and we are committed to prepare them for successful careers and further educational opportunities. More than half of our students come from low-income families and require assistance for essential schooling costs, such as transport and meals. Many of them work long hours in part-time jobs, which can affect their studies and their health. We appeal for your support to see these students from disadvantaged background through their ITE training, so that they can achieve their goals and aspirations. Your donations will fund bursaries for deserving students.

For more information, you may view this  [Endowment Fund Video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X-_0qOA0P9c) .

**Your gift is tax-deductible and matched by the Government**

Qualifying cash donations are eligible for 2.5 times tax deduction. All donations to ITE and the matched grants from the Government are directed to the ITE Education Fund, an Institution of Public Character (IPC) under a Management Committee appointed by the ITE Board of Governors.

You can donate online through  [FormSG](https://form.gov.sg/68b6a6a067df3bb546c6eb14)  or send us your gift together with this  [donation form [PDF, 111 KB]](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/8c310fa8-4b77-43e7-9529-771090642530/ite-education-fund-donation-form-mar2023.pdf) . For enquiries, please contact  [ief@ite.edu.sg](mailto:ief@ite.edu.sg) .

Keppel Care Foundation's gift to ITE at the Keppel Corporation's 50th Anniversary celebration

5. Address by Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi, Senior Parliamentary Secretary for Education & National Development, at the IgnITE Skills Challenge Finals 2026

Speech

# Address by Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi, Senior Parliamentary Secretary for Education & National Development, at the IgnITE Skills Challenge Finals 2026

26 May 2026

ITE College East
26 May 2026

Mr Peter Lam, CEO of ITE, Deputy CEOs, Principals,

Partners, Staff and Students of ITE and Secondary Schools, Ladies and Gentlemen,

1. A very good afternoon to all of you. Thank you for having me at this year's ignITE Skills Challenge Finals and Award Ceremony.

1. Today, we mark a special occasion — this year is the 10th edition of the ignITE Skills Challenge, and what a journey it has been. The ignITE Skills Challenge was launched in 2016 to encourage our students to learn more about applied learning, skills education, and hands-on problem-solving. From its humble beginnings, it has grown into a challenge that thousands of students look forward to each year.
2. This year, a total of 654 teams and over 1,900 students have participated. Many of you here are part of the final group that has gone on throughout the entire challenge today, and this is a testament to how meaningful and exciting this challenge is. To every single one of you — welcome, and well done for making it this far. Earlier, I had the opportunity to tour some of the challenge stations. I was genuinely impressed by the energy and creativity on display.

**Igniting Skills for the Future**

1. The overarching theme for 2026 is "Igniting Skills for the Future" — equipping our youths with agility, creativity, resilience and purpose, and preparing them for an evolving yet uncertain future. I think this theme is very timely.
2. Furthermore, this year’s challenges are organised around three forward-looking themes. The first, under Agility IgnITEd, challenges are centred on human science and wellness innovation. For example, the Pasta & Egg Challenge showcased how foundational skills in culinary arts were applied with precision, and adaptability. These highlight the importance of human-centred innovation, where technical competence is balanced with resilience and problem-solving.
3. In the area of Sustainability IgnITEd, challenges are centred on greenovation and sustainable design. For instance, Wild Wild Water and Re-ignITE Our Community Lah! demonstrated how students repurposed waste, designed with sustainability in mind, and reimagined inclusive community spaces, and this reflects a strong sense of environmental responsibility and social consciousness, traits vital for the next generation of innovators.
4. The third field of Technology IgnITEd look into the technology and intelligent systems. For example, X-Bots Extra illustrated how students applied robotics and coding to solve real-world problems — preparing our youths not just for Industry 4.0, but for a future where technology must be applied creatively, but responsibly.
5. These are examples of the skills that today's dynamic workplaces demand. Together, these themes encourage students to think holistically — not just about what they create, but why they create, for whom they design for, and how their solutions can improve lives and communities. That is a human-centred way of thinking, and one that will serve you well today, as well as tomorrow, and for the future, even in the age of AI.
6. As participants in these challenges, you have demonstrated your mastery of technical skills in the areas of human science & wellness innovation, greenovation & sustainable design, and technology & intelligent systems. But beyond the technical skills, the soft skills you displayed — creativity, critical thinking and teamwork – are all equally, if not more important, as skills that are critical in the workplace. The value of this experience is not in the final outcomes, but also in the process - in the journey that you have gone through thus far. What we have seen today is really months in the making, through the teamwork and effort that you have put in as a school, and the way you experimented, adapted to constraints, collaborated as teams, and learnt from failures. I hope you will continue to stay curious, keep learning, and make the most of opportunities like this as you explore your own interests and aspirations in the future.

**Conclusion**

1. Finally, an event of this scale is only possible through strong partnership, and I want to thank all the secondary schools, teachers and partners for your dedication and support. ITE plays a key role in our education system by providing students with a hands-on learning pathway, equipping them with work-ready skills and a strong foundation for not only now but for future upgrading — supporting the diverse strengths and aspirations of our students. To the ITE team behind this event, to have one event of this scale for one particular year is already a big achievement. But to be able to pull off ten wonderful years of IgnITE, to continue inspiring years and years of students, thousands of them who have gone through this programme is really a main feat. I want to give my sincere thanks to the ITE team for all that you do as part of lifting the confidence of our students and wanting to see them achieve their best potential.
2. And to all our participants and finalists — congratulations once again. I wish you all the best in your future journey. The future is indeed yours to ignite! Thank you.

Press Release

# ignITE Skills Challenge 2026: Igniting Passion for Future Careers

26 May 2026

Skills Challenge organised by ITE attracts highest ever participation

ITE’s IgnITE Skills Challenge 2026 has achieved its **record-breaking participation, with 1,962 secondary school students signing up** for the annual skills competition. Now in its tenth edition, the Challenge aims to introduce students to technical skills and foster a deeper understanding of the diverse courses offered by ITE.

Following the successful completion of the preliminary rounds from 13 to 16 April, the Finals took place today at ITE College East, where Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi, Senior Parliamentary Secretary, Ministry of Education and Ministry of National Development attended the event as Guest-of-Honour. Students showcased their skills by competing across 17 Skills Challenges, including **nine newly introduced Skills Challenges**focusing on the areas of sustainability, human science and advanced technologies. This is the largest number of Skills Challenges that has ever been included in series.

The nine new Skills Challenges are:

·       Biomechanics in Motion – Optimising Sports Performance

·       DermaRouge plus

·       Edible Ecofloat

·       HydroMotion: Green Grand Prix

·       PowerPlay: Fitness Data Quest

·       Re-ignITE Our Community Lah!

·       Speed Coding with Micro:bit

·       Trash to Trend: You Nailed it!

·       The Gripper X Innovation Quest

As a skills competition dedicated to secondary students, the ignITE Skills Challenge encourages participants to explore their potential through engaging and enjoyable challenges. This year, the Skills Challenges were categorised into three themes that align with Singapore’s future development plans: **Agility IgnITEd – Human Science & Wellness Innovation, Sustainability IgnITEd – Greenovation & Sustainable Design and Technology IgnITEd – Technology & Intelligent System**. Details of the Skills Challenges can be found in the **Annex**.

**Discovering Skills, Shaping Futures**

To prepare students for the Skills Challenges, participating students formed teams of three and either attended training workshops organised by ITE or enrolled in the ITE Applied Learning Module (ApLM@ITE) related to the Skills Challenge prior to the competition. The top three teams in each Skills Challenge received trophies and medals, while the school that excelled in the most challenges was awarded the prestigious Champion Trophy.

“It is encouraging to see how enthusiastically the students took on each Skills Challenge. All the Skills Challenges are linked to courses offered at ITE, and our hope is that through these engaging experiences, the students will discover new skills, uncover their interests and begin to envision the academic and career journeys they can chart with ITE,” said Mr Peter Lam, CEO, ITE.

Established in 2016, the IgnITE Skills Challenge has been organised by ITE with the support of Ministry of Education. For more information on ignITE Skills Challenge 2026, please visit:  [https://www.ite.edu.sg/ignite-skills-challenge-2026/](https://www.ite.edu.sg/ignite-skills-challenge-2026/)

[Click here for details on the 17 skill challenges [PDF, 219 KB]](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/d0e251e5-83bf-4c5b-98fe-1e779d97cfc9/ignite2026_skills-challenge.pdf)

5. Address by Dr Daniel Yip, BBS, JP, Deputy Chairman, VTC at Opening Ceremony of VTC-ITE International Student Seminar 2024

Speech

# Address by Dr Daniel Yip, BBS, JP, Deputy Chairman, VTC at Opening Ceremony of VTC-ITE International Student Seminar 2024

26 June 2024

VTC Auditorium
Hong Kong Design Institute
26 June 2024

Acting Chief Secretary Cheuk *(Mr CHEUK Wing-hing, Acting Chief Secretary for Administration of the HKSAR Government)*,

President Leung *(Hon Andrew LEUNG, President of Legislative Council)*,

LegCo Members,

Chairman Chong *(Mr Andrew CHONG, ITE Chairman)*

Khah Gek *(Ms LOW Khah Gek, ITE CEO)*,

ITE Friends,

Distinguished Speakers, Guests, Students, Ladies and Gentlemen,

Good morning!  I would like to extend a very warm welcome to you all to the VTC-ITE International Student Seminar 2024, especially to our guests, friends and over 300 students from the Institute of Technical Education (ITE) Singapore and Shenzhen Polytechnic University.

Today, we are very privileged to have Acting Chief Secretary for Administration, Mr Cheuk Wing-hing, gracing our event as our Guest of Honour.  We are also grateful to have the Honourable Andew Leung, President of the Legislative Council, LegCo Members and VTC Council Member, for joining us today.

VTC and ITE have been longstanding partners.  Sharing the same mission to provide young people with opportunities to acquire knowledge and skills for lifelong learning and enhanced employability, we have jointly organised this VTC-ITE International Student Seminar every two years since 2007.  The seminar has been a beacon of knowledge and interaction, engaging more than 4,000 students over the past 17 years in discussions on pressing global issues and honing their critical thinking skills.

This year, we embrace the theme “ISS Youth Change makers”, with sub-themes of “Innovation”, “Sustainability”, and “Social Impact” thoughtfully curated to ignite conversations on shaping a better future and contributing to our communities.  I believe our student participants will showcase their talent and creativity, and catalyse a movement to create lasting, powerful impact for generations to come.

Another exciting highlight of the programme will be the insightful sharing by our distinguished speakers on the seminar sub-themes.  We are pleased to have today :

- **Mr Edmund Lee**, Founder and CEO of AppTech, who will illuminate how disruptive innovations are reshaping our society for the better, and
- **Mr Mark Denis Ong,** Director of P&T Consultants, who will delve into sustainable construction practices vital for thriving in densely populated cities.

And Tomorrow, **Mr Ted Kwan,** Co-founder and CEO of Fullness Social Enterprises Society, will join us to share his first-hand experience in driving social change through social enterprises.

I trust this three-day programme will bring to our students inspiration for future career, and the opportunity to forge lasting friendships and networks amongst students from Singapore, Shenzhen and Hong Kong.  I do strongly encourage all students to seize this precious opportunity to immerse in diverse cultures and broaden your perspectives.

As I bring my remarks to a close, I would like to express my heartfelt appreciation to our great partner, ITE, for its full support to this Seminar; and also to all the students for your enthusiastic engagement.  I wish you all a rewarding and enjoyable experience.

Thank you.

5. Address by Dr Janil Puthucheary, Senior Minister of State, at the Work-Study Diploma Graduation Ceremony

Speech

# Address by Dr Janil Puthucheary, Senior Minister of State, at the Work-Study Diploma Graduation Ceremony

12 November 2025

ITE Headquarters
12 November 2025

Mr Andrew Chong, Chairman, ITE

Ms Low Khah Gek, CEO, ITE

Members of the ITE Board of Governors

Employers and Company Representatives

Graduands and Parents

Ladies and Gentlemen

1.            Good morning. I am very glad to join you at this year’s ITE Work-Study Diploma Graduation Ceremony.

2.            Congratulations to the 892 Work-Study Diploma graduands from the Class of 2025! You should all be very proud of your personal and professional growth on this journey.

a. I also want to give special mention to the 57 top graduands among you, who will be receiving course medals for your outstanding performance. Well done!

**Positive Outcomes for ITE Work-Study Diploma Graduates**

3.            The ITE Work-Study Diploma programme provides an applied educational pathway for trainees to learn not just through classroom instruction, but also through substantial on-the-job training. Employer mentors and trainers play a key role to equip trainees with knowledge and skills, alongside our dedicated ITE lecturers.

a.    In this way, our trainees gain valuable work experience, and a head start in their careers, together with the skills that they learn. And as full-time employees, you also earn a salary while studying.

b.    Employers benefit too, with a pipeline of talent that can address skills and manpower shortages. And because the Work-Study Diploma course curriculum is co-developed by ITE and the employers, the training can directly address each employer’s needs.

4.            So, I am very glad to see that the take-up of the Work-Study Diploma has grown significantly over the years, and it has delivered concrete and positive outcomes for our graduates.

a.    The Work-Study Diploma began in 2018 with just 4 courses and 100 trainees. Today, there are more than 40 courses available and the annual intake is more than 1,600 trainees in 2025 – and more than 700 employer partners.

b.    The latest graduate employment survey shows that WorkStudy Diploma graduates earn a median monthly starting salary of $2,975 – this figure has been rising steadily over the years and matches the earnings of full-time polytechnic diploma graduates. It is a significant increase compared to trainees’ initial median monthly salary of $2,000 when they first started this programme. This shows the value of the skills you have learnt, and your ability to take on higherlevel jobs and tasks.

5.            I am going to share two stories. These two individuals are exemplars and role models who represent all of you, in integrating working and studying.

a.    The first story is about,**Ms Yvette Tan**. Congratulations to Yvette who is graduating today with a **Work-Study Diploma in Community Engagement & Development**.

Yvette first discovered her passion for social services while interning at a school for children with special needs. She  pursued her passion as a Work-Study Diploma trainee with **Inclus Pte Ltd**, where she supported Persons with Disabilities. Inclus later selected her to be a Main Lifeskill coach at the newly established InSchool Special Needs Student Care Centre – this is a responsibility typically taken on by more experienced employees. In acknowledgement of her excellence in both the workplace and classroom, Yvette is receiving the Gold Course Medal today, an award given to the top trainee in each course. Congratulations and well done, Yvette!

b.    My second story is about **Ms Qistina Masyitah Binte Mazlan**. She is receiving her **Work-Study Diploma in Architectural Building Information Modeling (BIM) & Design**today. Congratulations Masyitah! With her skills in BIM software, she was selected to represent ITE at the WorldSkills Singapore 2025 Competition where she earned a Medallion of Excellence.  After graduation, she is continuing on with her Work-Study Diploma employer, **Kyoob Architects Pte Ltd**, where she has contributed meaningfully to complex BIM tasks on projects such as the upcoming Tanglin Halt Polyclinic and Costa Riviera HDB BTO development. Looking ahead, she is hoping to pursue a degree in Landscape Architecture, to build on her WorkStudy Diploma. Once again, congratulations Masyitah for your work and your excellence!

**Importance of Industry Partners and Mentors in Co-delivering Work-Study Diplomas**

6.            The achievements and strong outcomes of our Work-Study Diploma graduates would not be possible without the dedication of our industry partners and mentors, many of whom are present here today.

a.    I thank all of you for guiding and supporting our trainees – starting from attending ITE’s Train-the-Trainer programme. The trainers and the employers – they have to go back and learn as well, in order to be able to support this programme. This ensures that our trainers have the necessary skills to deliver meaningful workplace training. Thank you for putting in the hours to nurture and train them.

7.            So, it is very fitting that we are recognising 11 outstanding mentors at today’s ceremony, with the Advanced Certified Industry Trainer Certificate.

a.    One recipient is **Ms Norhidayah Binte Jamsuri** from **Sathya Sai Social Service**. Thank you Ms Norhidayah for being here today and for committing to this important work. She tailors her teaching methods to different learner profiles and implements structured systems to benefit the trainers and the trainees at her workplace – and these are skills that she picked up from ITE’s Train-the-Trainer programme.

b.    Congratulations and thank you to all our outstanding mentors!

**Growing The Work-Study Diploma Programme**

8.            We want to continue growing the Work-Study Diploma pathway. I am happy to share that ITE will be launching a new Work-Study Diploma in Advanced Manufacturing in 2026. This will equip trainees to drive innovation in modern manufacturing, including designing and producing precision components using advanced technologies and computer-aided design tools.

9.            ITE will also be launching a new Wholesale Trade specialisation for the Work-Study Diploma in Integrated Supply Chain Management, as an addition to the existing Logistics specialisation. Given Singapore’s role as a global trading and logistics hub, we want to help more trainees take up good jobs in the sector. This dual specialisation will allow trainees to choose the path that best suits their needs, while they gain an understanding of how both functions interconnect to optimise supply chain efficiency.

10.        Beyond launching new programmes, I am also glad that ITE and community partners are working together to provide both prospective and currently enrolled ITE Work-Study Diploma trainees with enhanced career mentoring support and resources, over and above the mentorship provided by their employers.

a.    Earlier this year, ITE launched the **JumpStart mentoring initiative** in collaboration with **Quantedge Foundation Singapore** and the local career guidance charity, **The Astronauts Collective**. ITE Higher Nitec final-year students taking part in internships, applicants for Work-Study Diplomas, and Work-Study Diploma first-year students – these three groups can tap on this initiative to seek support from industry professionals who volunteer as career mentors. So, this is part of that support and resources for career mentoring, how to make the right choices for the pathway that suits your training needs.

b.    One example is **Mr Soh Weng Hong**, a **Work-Study Diploma in Facilities Management trainee**. He shared how his JumpStart mentor, **Ms Lim Yu Xian**, a Building Infrastructure Manager in the sector, has made a real difference. Yu Xian offers him encouragement and advice in adapting to the steep learning curve of his new job when he is tackling a challenging project. It’s very important to give that mentorship and scaffolding. Beyond the information that is provided, it’s also about the relationship, the advice, and the role modelling that a mentor provides to a trainee, as the trainee is finding their way into the workforce, finding out about themselves and their aptitude.

So, thank you to all our mentors for doing this.

**Conclusion**

11.          To conclude, let me thank ITE and our industry partners once again for your efforts in supporting our Work-Study Diploma trainees, and in expanding this very meaningful educational pathway. I urge all our industry partners to continue strengthening your talent development pipeline through the Work-Study Diploma programme, and go and tell your partners, colleagues and friends in the industry. We want to welcome more companies to come on board and make more pathways available for our trainees

12.          To our graduands, today marks not just an achievement, but the celebration of your hard work, excellence and the beginning of your new journey. Carry forward the determination and resilience that you have and that have brought you to this moment. Remain curious learners, seek out new opportunities for growth, and create meaningful contributions in all of your chosen fields.

13.          Once again, congratulations to the Class of 2025!

14.          Thank you very much.

5. Address by Guest of Honour Mr Shawn Huang, Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the Ministry of Education, at the ITE-Tall Ship Adventures MOU Signing Ceremony

Speech

# Address by Guest of Honour Mr Shawn Huang, Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the Ministry of Education, at the ITE-Tall Ship Adventures MOU Signing Ceremony

24 July 2024

The Royal Albatross
24 July 2024

Mr Peter Pela, CEO of Tall Ship Adventures

Ms Low Khah Gek, CEO of ITE

Industry partners

Ladies and gentlemen

1. A very good evening. It is my pleasure to celebrate the MOU signing between ITE and Tall Ship Adventures (TSA), which had earlier taken place on board the special setting of the Royal Albatross.

**Embracing Growth**

1. Luxury vessels like the Royal Albatross showcase the dynamism of Singapore’s maritime ecosystem, which has evolved from a humble trading post to a maritime hub offering a comprehensive suite of services.
2. This evolution can be charted in the history of Keppel Bay, which started out as a small harbour in the mid-1800s before becoming a bustling shipyard in the 1900s, supporting the brisk sea trade that accelerated Singapore’s economic success. With the move of Keppel Shipyard to Tuas in 1996, Keppel Bay is now a vibrant waterfront precinct.
3. This transformation story speaks to the importance of embracing growth in the face of changing winds.
4. I congratulate TSA for doing the same, in seeking new horizons and uncovering new opportunities. In 2015, TSA entered Singapore’s waters to provide a unique dinner cruise experience aboard Asia’s only luxury tall ship. Today, TSA will unveil its expansion plan, adding new and exciting experiences to the diverse slate of attractions in Singapore.

**Elevating the Human Touch in the Hospitality Sector**

1. Companies across the hospitality sector are embracing growth. Riding on the wave of digital transformation, the sector is finding new ways to automate, streamline and refine business processes with the use of emerging technologies. AI, for instance, is powering personalised guest experiences, from chatbot assistance for reservations, to predictive analytics to understand consumer behaviour, anticipate needs, and thereby boost customer loyalty.
2. However, in a sector that thrives on social interactions, the human touch remains vital and irreplaceable. Intelligent as AI is, it cannot replicate the authenticity and empathy that is key to human connection. Amid increasing digitalisation, the value of high-touch hospitality has thus become more pronounced, and the need to balance high technology with high touch service even more paramount.
3. Students pursuing a hospitality career should therefore not only retain, but also elevate the human touch by honing their customer-facing skills. This is best achieved through hands-on training in the workplace.
4. Industry attachments such as those offered by TSA play a critical role in our students’ training and development. Over the past ten years, more than 120 students from the Higher Nitec in Passenger Services have benefitted from these opportunities. With the guidance of skilled mentors, students have gained firsthand experience in managing frontof-house operations and F&B services on board the Royal Albatross, sharpening their technical and soft skills to prepare for successful careers in the sector. The renewal of TSA’s partnership with ITE will provide more internship opportunities for our students.
5. TSA will also award up to 16 scholarships every year, enabling students to attain the relevant professional certificates, including the Royal Albatross Passenger Handling Certificate and Workforce Skills Qualification (WSQ) Food Safety certification. I am extremely encouraged by TSA’s long-standing partnership with ITE, and confident that our students will continue to benefit from these immersive learning experiences.

**Delivering Industry-Focussed Training at ITE**

1. Today’s MOU signing highlights ITE’s priority of delivering industry-focused training, by leveraging a wide network of over 5,000 industry stakeholders like TSA. With the ongoing roll-out of the enhanced threeyear curricular structure leading directly to a Higher Nitec, many industry partners have come on board to co-design and co-deliver ITE’s curriculum. All students will go through two industry attachments, to deepen students’ industry-relevant skillsets, and build a strong foundation for work and further upskilling.
2. Such close collaboration between our institutions and industry benefit both parties. Institutions are able to equip students with future-forward skillsets in authentic workplace settings, while companies can enjoy the first pick of promising students and benefit from a steady pipeline of industry-ready talent.
3. Beyond this, industry attachments also facilitate mutual discovery between companies and students. Companies can get to know and discover the goals and needs of future employees, while tapping on fresh perspectives to explore new boundaries. At the same time, students have the opportunity to gain insight into companies’ ethos and ambitions.
4. Take for example Yuvashri, or Shri for short. Shri joined the Royal Albatross crew on her industry attachment in 2023, and put to practice what she had learnt about passenger handling and customer interaction. Her experiences in engaging a wide variety of guests honed her interpersonal and communication skills. At the same time, TSA also tapped on Shri’s creativity and familiarity with trends to customise themed events for younger guests. This allowed TSA to attract new clients, and more importantly, engage a new client base.
5. Recognising and valuing her contributions, TSA offered Shri a role in TSA after her graduation. Shri was happy to take up the opportunity, as she enjoyed TSA’s collaborative work culture, and felt that she could contribute to and grow more in the company.
6. Building on the soft skills that she picked up during her industry attachment, Shri has since acquired new business knowledge, and successfully navigated diverse job roles on board the Royal Albatross, from front-of-house operations to logistics management.
7. Shri’s journey highlights the importance and lasting impact of these industry attachments. By incorporating the latest industry know-how into the ITE curriculum, we not only boost individuals’ careers, but also enhance the quality of Singapore’s workforce and businesses.
8. Mr Peta Pela, founder and CEO of Tallship Adventures, your journey is an inspiring one. You have spent most of your career in IT, but that does not hinder you from pursuing new ventures and adventure. And from your passion of fishing, diving, and sailing, you have built an attraction and travel experience that Singapore is indeed very proud of.
9. TSA won the Singapore Tourism Board’s Outstanding Attraction Experience Award in 2022 and achieved Tripadvisor’s Travelers’ Choice Awards Best of the Best – awarded only to the top 1% of attractions worldwide. Let’s give a round of applause to congratulate Peta’s success.
10. Such an achievement is no easy feat. Together with TSA, amongst all of us today, are numerous industry partners. You understand the journey and the effort required to achieve high global quality standards and build a successful venture. Creating an ecosystem, sustaining it and staying relevant for the future.
11. Where we are today, standing amongst friends, was once known as *Pulau Belakang Mati*. It was an island with many *kampungs*, and mainly pineapple plantations – with little or no economic activity. But today, much has changed.
12. It’s been more than 50 years since the work to build the Southern Island paradise begun, and Sentosa – also known as the island of tranquility, has undergone dramatic changes. This is only possible because of the hard work of each generation, putting together the building blocks essential in transforming a little island into a global destination.

**Conclusion**

1. Like any endeavor, any vision would require determination, dedicated effort, and collaboration with all stakeholders to succeed. So as TSA and ITE embark on their nextbound of collaboration, I invite all industry partners here to partner our Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs), to grow and secure our next generation of talent. Such collaborations will help to keep our workforce and businesses nimble, vibrant and dynamic – all of which will drive our economy to greater heights.
2. Once again, thank you TSA for your partnership, and I wish ITE and TSA every success in their continued collaboration.

Thank you very much.
