# ITE Student Code of Conduct

The ITE Student Code of Conduct sets out the standards of conduct expected of our students.

Last updated 9 December 2025

ITE is committed to the holistic development of our students. As part of this commitment, we work at instilling integrity, encouraging right decision-making, and fostering self-accountability among students. Being a responsible member of ITE community, we believe that it is our personal responsibility to act in accordance with all institutional rules and policies. The ITE Student Code of Conduct sets out the standards of conduct expected of our students.  It is to create a safe, harmonious and enjoyable learning experience in ITE where every student can grow and develop, in an inclusive environment within and outside of the campus, to uphold the good reputation of ITE at all times. The ITE Student Code of Conduct is binding on all students/trainees and all students/trainees are required to comply with it at all times.

## Attire

- Full-time students must be properly attired in ITE uniform or prescribed attire while in College during term time and at all ITE-organised activities, events or functions, including co-curricular activities.
- All Traineeship, Work-Study Diploma students, and CET students attending day classes at ITE must respect the decorum of ITE, and be properly and decently attired.
- Students should carry with them their student cards for identification while in campus.
- Modification to the uniform or prescribed attire and improper dressing (eg. wearing caps or other non-prescribed headgear, slippers, provocative clothing) are prohibited.
- Male students must be clean-shaven and not sport long hair or wear ear rings / ear studs in the College.
- Students should not sport hair in outrageous colours (for example blue, green, purple, red, ash etc.).
- Students should not display any tattoos outwardly.  All tattoos must be covered up appropriately.
- Students attending workshops/laboratories must wear proper attire and safety shoes/footwear.

## Attendance

- Students are required to attend and be punctual for all scheduled lessons, workshops or laboratory sessions and official ITE and College functions.
- Students who are absent from lessons or official functions must produce a medical certificate or obtain official leave approval.

## Behaviour

- Students should be thoughtful towards others, and show respect for the culture, language, race and religion of fellow students, staff and members of the community, both within and outside of ITE.
- Students should be respectful and courteous in their behaviour towards lecturers, other ITE staff, including company supervising staff for Traineeship, Work-Study Diploma and internship.
- Students should not commit acts of disturbance within or outside of ITE’s premises.
- Students should refrain from bullying or any behaviour that is harmful, intimidating, humiliating, immoral or indecent towards others.  This also applies to all hazing activities, even where the other person has expressed willingness to participate in the activities.
- Students should avoid acts which will bring disrepute to themselves and ITE, or are harmful towards good order and discipline in the Colleges.
- Students should comply with and observe any such rules and regulations as may be made from time to time by the College.
- Students should not commit criminal offences punishable by law.

## Sexual misconduct

- Sexual misconduct (including but not limited to sexual assault, outrage of modesty, voyeuristic acts) will not be tolerated.
- Students should not engage in any act of sexual misconduct whether in the form of an action, or words, verbal or in writing, including on any non-digital or digital media.
- Students should not display or be in possession of any pornographic materials, which includes sexually explicit images on clothing, pictures screen savers, videos, posters or objects.
- Students must also refrain from sending or forwarding sexually explicit e-mails, videos, notes or messages through SMS / WhatsApp / other social media.

## Littering

- Students should not litter, and keep the campus clean at all times.  Trash should be disposed of into the disposal bins.
- Students should not consume drink or eat in the class/ laboratory/ workshop/ library.
- Students should return all utensils to the respective receptacles provided within the cafeteria.

## College property

- Students should not damage, vandalise, steal or lose any ITE property.
- Any loss or damage to property belonging to the College must be reported immediately.
- Students are to refrain from removing/moving any property that belongs to the College unless authorised.
- Students are to return any items found in the College premises to the Customer & Visitor Centre.

## Social media

- Students are to act responsibly when using and communicating through social media platforms, social networking sites, video and photo-sharing sites.
- Students are expected to conduct themselves in an objective and respectful manner in the cyber and digital space.
- Students are expected to be mindful of the contents that they post in public domains and ensure that their messages are not offensive, racist, vulgar and/or threatening.
- Harassment and cyberbullying on social media targeting at an individual with malicious insults or intents are strictly prohibited.

## Smoking and Vaping

- Students should not smoke or be in possession of cigarettes / any tobacco products while in ITE premises as they are gazetted as NON SMOKING areas.
- Students must not vape or purchase/ possess, distribute, sell, import e-vaporisers (including those containing etomidate) as vaping is illegal in Singapore.
- Students wearing the ITE uniform or prescribed attire are prohibited from smoking within or outside of ITE’s premises.

## Academic integrity

- ITE does not tolerate any form of academic dishonesty.  Academic dishonesty includes, but is not limited to, cheating, plagiarism, forgery and violation of intellectual property and copyright laws.
- Students who are found cheating during examinations will be disciplined according to the ITE Examination Rules & Regulations.
- Plagiarism occurs when you copy a piece of work or AI-generated output and pass it off as your own without acknowledgement of the source of information.
- Forging or possession of forged official documents is a serious offence with severe consequences.
- Unauthorised use or illegal copying of copyright materials including printed and/or non-printed matters and computer software or the disclosure of computer passwords to others is a serious offence.
- For information relating to examinations and absence, please refer to ITE Examination Rules & Regulations.

## Gambling

- Students must not engage in any form of gambling (including online gambling or e-gambling) in ITE’s premises.
- Any form of card games, using poker or any other cards associated with gambling is prohibited in ITE’s premises.

## Alcohol, drugs and inhalant abuse

- Students must not be in possession and / or engage in consumption of alcoholic drinks or intoxicating substances on campus.
- Drugs are illegal in Singapore.  Students must not be in possession, or engage in consumption, trafficking or manufacturing of drugs.
- Students must not engage in inhalant abuse.

## Fighting, assault or possession of dangerous weapons

- Students must not be involved in fighting, assault or be in possession of dangerous weapons.

## Global education

Students participating in Overseas Exposure Programme (OEP) are deemed as ambassadors of ITE and Singapore, and must uphold the highest standards of conduct and behaviour at all times.

### Country’s law and culture

**Each country has their own unique customs and laws. When overseas, students should:**

- Be aware of and comply with the laws of the host country.
- Be respectful, sensitive and open-minded towards local cultures and norms.
- Abide by the dress and cultural codes of the host country.
- Be sensitive to gender and cultural differences, languages, political affinities and religious beliefs.
- Refrain from participating in any illegal activity.

**Should students be unclear of the customs and cultures of the land, they should consult their lecturers or lectures/leaders from the host country.**

E-vaporisers (including those containing etomidate) and Vaping are illegal in Singapore. Students caught at land, air or sea checkpoints in possession of e-vaporisers, will be liable for the penalty imposed for importation of e-vaporisers.

### Conduct when overseas

**For your own well-being and personal safety when overseas, students should not:**

- Purchase, possess or consume any form of drugs even if it is legal in the host country.
- Purchase or possess dangerous weapons and firearms even if it is legal in the host country.
- Purchase, use, possess or consume any cannabis-infused food products, vaping paraphernalia (eg., e-vaporisers), or purchase weapon-like items during overseas trips. Bringing such contraband items back to Singapore from overseas carries potentially heavier penalties, if caught.
- Share a room between male and female students.
- Operate or rent any form of motorised vehicle.
- Visit adult entertainment establishments such as bars, pubs, clubs, KTV, massage parlours, etc.
- Engage in high-risk/dangerous activities (eg. sky-diving, shooting range, cave diving, white-water rafting, etc).
- Cross over international borders unless it is part of the official programme.
- Consume alcohol.
- Engage in inappropriate behaviour, such as lewdness, drunkenness, intimidation, threats, violence, fighting and immoral/indecent activities.

## Disciplinary matters

If a student is aware of another student acting in violation of the ITE Student Code of Conduct, the student is expected to report the suspected misconduct to his or her academic school staff (Lecturers, Class Advisor, Managers, Section Heads, Student Guidance Officers) as soon as possible.

Students who fail to abide by the Code of Conduct or commit disciplinary offences are liable to disciplinary actions by Colleges. Students who do not meet the required attendance rate may be debarred from taking the examinations. Where ITE property is damaged or lost, students may be required to compensate ITE for the loss or damage where appropriate. Students involved in criminal offences / illegal activities will also be reported to the Police.All ITE staff are empowered to enforce discipline on campus. The School management/School Discipline Committee has the authority to take disciplinary action and if necessary, refer offenders to the College Disciplinary Committee (CDC).

For students who have committed serious disciplinary offences, the CDC may impose one or more of the following penalties:

1. Manual and/or course-related work;
2. Verbal and/or written warnings;
3. Temporary suspension from classes;
4. Dismissal from College;
5. Withdrawal of privileges; and
6. Fine and/ or Community Service Order (CSO)

Students who are dismissed or suspended for more than one week may seek an appeal within 7 days. An independent Appeals Review Panel/ Appeals Committee will be convened to review the appeal received.  The decision by the Appeals Review Panel/ Appeals Committee, after reviewing the case, shall be final.  Where a student has been convicted of a criminal offence or has been proven to have misconducted himself or has committed acts outside the institute premises that will or are likely to bring disrepute to the ITE, the CDC may consider the investigation report of the police and/or such other law enforcement authority and/or record of the proceedings of the court, and take any necessary actions as it deems fit, including temporary suspension or dismissal of the student.

## Conclusion

The ITE Student Code of Conduct, which is not meant to be exhaustive in scope, will help to remind students of the standards set to foster a College environment which everyone can be proud of.  The students’ commitment to these standards contributes to the good image of ITE and a pleasant environment for everyone.

# Certification system

ITE offers Full-time, Part-time, and Work-Study programmes with certifications to support education and workforce upskilling needs.

Last updated 27 August 2025

## Full-time education

- **National ITE Certificate (*****Nitec*****)** for courses that require completion of GCE ‘N’ Level or GCE ‘O’ Level as an entry requirement, with pre-requisites for certain courses.
- **Higher National ITE Certificate (*****Higher Nitec*****)** for courses that require GCE ‘O’ Level or GCE 'N' (Academic) Level with pre-requisites as an entry requirement.
- **Technical Diploma** for courses that require relevant *Higher Nitec* / *Nitec* as an entry requirement.

## Traineeship programmes

- Some*Nitec* and *Higher Nitec* courses are offered in traineeship mode as well. Entry requirements are similar to related courses in full-time education.

## Work-Study programmes

- **Work-Study Diploma**for courses that are in partnership with employers targeted at ITE Graduates with relevant *Higher Nitec* / *Nitec* or relevant working experience as an entry requirement.

## Part-time education

- **National ITE Certificate (*****Nitec*****)** for courses that cater to the upgrading needs of the workforce, and require completion of GCE ‘N’ Level or GCE ‘O’ Level as an entry requirement, with pre-requisites for certain courses.
- **Higher National ITE Certificate (*****Higher Nitec*****)** for courses that cater to the upgrading needs of the workforce, and require GCE ‘O’ Level or GCE 'N' (Academic) Level with pre-requisites as an entry requirement.
- **ITE Skills Certificate (ISC)**for courses that cater to the upgrading needs of the workforce.
- **SkillsFuture Series Certificate of Competency (COC)**for short courses that provide industry-relevant training in emerging and critical skills areas, comprising beginner to intermediate to advance levels.
- **Train The Trainer programme (TTT)**prepares trainers and On-the-Job Training practitioners to effectively instruct, coach, assess, and develop curriculum and assessments for industry training.

# Counselling services

Student Care @ ITE Colleges

Last updated 7 July 2026

## Find comfort and support at ITE's welcoming campus

At ITE, we understand that not all wounds are visible, and sometimes, life can be tough. Our campus offers a warm and welcoming environment where you can find the support you need. Our friendly counsellors are always ready to listen and help you through any challenges you might face. In cosy and comfortable settings, you can talk openly about your feelings and worries. We are here to support you and make sure things get better.

## Your safe space for open conversations

Our counsellors follow a strict confidentiality policy, ensuring that you have a safe space to share your thoughts. You can trust that your conversations will remain private, allowing you to speak freely. The only exception is if there is a serious risk to someone's life, in which case we must act to keep everyone safe. We want you to feel secure and supported as you navigate through any difficulties.

# Financial assistance

Find out more about the financial assistance schemes are available to support Singaporean full-time students.

Last updated 30 April 2026

## A) ITE Monthly Financial Assistance Scheme (MFAS) and Special Student Assistance Scheme (SSAS)

The **MFAS** provides a monthly allowance to eligible students who need regular financial support for daily expenses. The scheme provides $200 per month and number of months of award shall be assessed by the College based on the student’s needs and the funds available.

The **SSAS** provides a one-time financial aid to eligible students who need help to tide over short-term financial difficulties or a sudden financial crisis in the family. The scheme ranges from $300 to $600, and shall be assessed by the College based on the student’s needs and the funds available.

**Application for Bursary & Financial Assistance**

To apply for the above bursaries and financial assistance, the student should submit an on-line application for financial assistance and supporting income documents, (e.g. latest payslips, income tax assessment, etc.) for verification and inform his College should there be a change in his household income after application during the academic year. He will be informed if his bursary application is successful. Successful applicants will receive the bursary award via PayNow NRIC or Giro.

Student will be required to refund the full or partial bursary quantum if he is dismissed or voluntarily withdraws or defers from his course of study or is in receipt of a full scholarship/sponsorship/bursary that covers tuition fees and provides an annual or monthly living allowance.

For more information on how to apply for Bursary & Financial Assistance, please click  [here [PDF,743 KB]](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/c7a7f637-986d-483a-9766-a19bccd726c0/Step By Step Guide on Applying Financial Assistance_Bursary_15 Sep 25.pdf) .

## B) Opportunity Fund (OF)

The **OF** provides a subsidy to eligible students to purchase IT device for their studies. The subsidy is up to 80% of the cost of the IT device, capped at $1,100.

If the student is eligible, he can claim the subsidy if he is an active student at the time of claim and have not claimed a similar subsidy in the last three years.

He can purchase his device from any local retail shop or ITE-approved vendors. For purchase at a local retail shop, he will need to submit his receipt and invoice to the Student Services Centre of the College within one month of purchase, to receive his subsidy credited directly into his bank account.

Alternatively, he may purchase the laptop from any of the ITE**-**approved vendors where he only need to pay the difference in price after subsidy.

List of approved vendors

The following is a list of ITE approved vendors where the student will only need to pay the difference in price after subsidy:

1. *AsiaPac Technology Pte Ltd & NUS Co-op*

- [HP ITE e-shop (subsidised)](https://e-shop-hp.asiapac.com.sg/)
- [Lenovo ITE e-shop (subsidised)](https://e-shop-lenovo.asiapac.com.sg/)
2. *Acer Computer (Singapore) Pte Ltd*

- [Acer ITE e-shop (subsidised)](https://store.acer.com/en-sg/ite)

**Example A**: If the listed price of the PC/Laptop/Tablet is $1,300 Listed price = $1,300 80% x $1,300 = $1,040 The student pay 20% ($1,300 - $1,040) = $260

As 80% of the purchase price did not exceed the subsidy cap of S$1,100, the student is only required to pay the remaining 20%. In this case, he will need to pay the vendor $260. ITE will pay the subsidy of $1,040 directly to the vendor.

**Example B**: If the listed price of the PC/Laptop/Tablet is $1,400 Listed price = $1,400 80% x $1,400 = $1,120 (Exceeded subsidy of $1,100) The student pay ($1,400 - $1,100) = $300

Although 80% of the purchase price is $1,120, it has exceeded the subsidy cap of $1,100. Hence he will need to pay the vendor $300. ITE will pay the subsidy of $1,100 directly to the vendor.

Please select Payment Method as "FAS" or "PC SUBSIDY" when order online.

Important: The student will need to liaise directly with the vendor for any enquires on and not limited to ordering, delivering, warranty, specs, payment or cancellation.

ITE will not be responsible for any disputes between student and vendor.If the student is awarded an external IT grant from other organisation to purchase IT device during the academic year, he will need to declare this to the College and refund the OF subsidy received.

## F) Deferment of National Service (NS) for NS-Liable Males

NS-liable males will be granted NS deferment for the pursuit of full-time studies at pre-university government-funded institutions including ITE if they attain a place and are pursuing a course for higher academic qualifications from what they have previously attained (e.g. from N/O Levels to *Nitec*/*Higher Nitec*, from *Nitec* to *Higher Nitec* or from *Nitec*/*Higher Nitec* to ITE Work-Study Diploma/Technical Engineer Diploma/Technical Diploma courses) and NS deferment will no longer be subject to cut-off ages. # Application for ITE Student Concession Card (New student)

If you are a new student enrolling at ITE for the first time, you will need to submit a recent photo to obtain your ITE Student Concession Card.

Last updated 30 April 2026

## A) What do I need to upload?

The photo must:

- Be in colour, taken against plain white background without shadow
- Be taken within the last 3 months
- Show the full face without headgear (see sample photo below)
- Show that your hair is neatly combed or tied up and must be of natural colour and not showing any jewellery.

Do ensure that your photo image file meets these SimplyGo’s requirements: a) The photo must be saved in this format: **NRIC.jpg** (e.g. T1234567A.jpg) b) The dimension of the photo image must be **240 x 320 pixels** c) The file size should be about **150KB****Do note that you cannot change the photo once submitted.**

Click  [here [PDF, 95 KB]](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/37e0c9a9-baa4-4743-8fce-47e28a027411/tools-to-resize-photo.pdf)  for tools to resize the photo that meets the above criteria.

## B) How do I upload my photograph image?

If you need to upload your photo after course acceptance, you can do so online at  [Photo submission for student concession card](https://student.ite.edu.sg)  (Click Student Admissions tab >> FAS/Photo/PSEA), 2 working days after accepting your course.

*Highly recommended to use****Google Chrome****to upload your photo for seamless submission.*

*Do note that Google , Google Go and Google Chrome are different platforms.*

## C) When do I need to upload?

You should upload your photo during course acceptance or within the **first three weeks** after the term begins.

Eligible students graduating in 2025 can enjoy four more months of concessionary fares by extending their Concession cards between 1 January 2025 and 31 December 2025 at any of the Ticketing Machines or Counters as listed below:

- SimplyGo Kiosk
- Top-Up Kiosk
- SimplyGo Ticket Office / Ticketing Service Centre (TSC)
- Passenger Service Centre

6. Replacement of expired or lost ITE Student Concession

# Replacement of expired or lost ITE Student Concession

Find out how to replace your expired or lost ITE Student Concession Card.

Last updated 30 April 2026

## A) Replacement of expired ITE Student Concession Card

To replace an expired ITE Student Concession Card, visit the College’s Student Services Centre to collect an **Appendix H Form.**With this form, you can apply for an immediate replacement at any SimplyGo Ticketing Service Centre (TSC). Please note that SimplyGo will charge a replacement fee.

## B) Replacement of lost ITE Student Concession Card

To replace a lost ITE Student Concession Card, contact SimplyGo at 1800-2255-663 to arrange for an immediate replacement at any Ticketing Service Centre (TSC). Please bring the following:

- Original NRIC/Passport for Singapore citizens or Original NRIC/Re-entry Permit for Singapore Permanent Residents or Original Student Pass (FIN) for international students
- One recent colored passport-size photo taken within the last 3 months (see photo requirements below) or School Smartcard (if applicable); and
- A replacement fee along with a minimum top-up travel value of $5

The photo must:

- Be in colour, taken against plain white background without shadow
- Be taken within the last 3 months
- Show the full face without headgear (see sample photo on the left)
- Show that your hair is neatly combed or tied up and must be of natural colour
- Not showing any jewellery

## C) Locations of SimplyGo Ticketing Service Centres (TSCs)

The TSCs are located at:

- Admiralty MRT Station
- Ang Mo Kio Bus Interchange
- Bukit Panjang MRT Station*
- Buona Vista MRT Station
- Choa Chu Kang Bus Interchange
- Hougang Bus Interchange
- Jurong East Interim Bus Interchange
- Marine Parade MRT Station
- Maxwell MRT Station
- Somerset MRT Station*
- Tampines Bus Interchange

Operating Hours: 10am to 6pm daily. Closed on Public Holidays.

*Bukit Panjang and Somerset TSCs will be closed for meal break from 2pm to 3pm.

Besides TSCs, students who have lost their concession cards may also choose to replace their cards via SimplyGo online e-Services. For further details, please click  [here](https://www.simplygo.com.sg/concession-monthly-travel-cards/?tab=pills-CardReplacement-tab) .

# Learning accessibility

Experience personalised support at ITE's Learning Accessibility Office (LAO).

Last updated 30 April 2026

At ITE, each college has a special place called the Learning Accessibility Office (LAO). This is where students with Special Education Needs (SEN) get the help they need to succeed in their studies. Our staff work closely with students to make sure they have a well-rounded education. We focus on helping students develop important skills for living independently and finding meaningful jobs after they graduate.

## A) Services available

Students with special needs can approach the LAO at their respective Colleges for assistance to access services needed for their learning, such as:

- Course counselling
- Transition support
- Advice on Assistive Technology Devices
- Access to facilities
- Behavioural support
- Provision of appropriate access arrangements during tests and examinations
- Industrial attachment
- Career Counselling

## B) Locations of LAOs

- ITE College Central : Student Care @ Central, Block A, Level 3, Unit 08 [How to get here](/about-ite/colleges/college-central/locate-us/)
- ITE College East : Student Care Department, Admin Block, Level 2, A02-02 [How to get here](/about-ite/colleges/college-east/locate-us/)
- ITE College West : Student Care Department, Block 3, Level 6 [How to get here](/about-ite/colleges/college-west/locate-us/)

## C) Reach out and get the support you need at ITE

If you have special needs, we encourage you to contact the College Learning Accessibility Office (LAO) when you enrol in an ITE course. This way, we can guide you on the support available to help you succeed. By sharing your learning needs, we can ensure you have the right support from the start. Rest assured, your personal information will be kept private and only shared with your consent, unless required by law or for safety reasons.

It is important to let us know about any special learning needs you have so that we could provide the right services for you and help you make your education journey in ITE smoother and more enjoyable.

## D) SEN Fund

The MOE SEN Fund helps students with (1) physical and sensory (i.e. hearing & visual) conditions, (2) learning & language conditions, or (3) social and behavioural conditions to purchase Assistive Technology devices and supporting services. Examples of Assistive Technology devices and support services include the following:

- Alternative keyboards
- Braille displays
- Braille printers / embossers
- Computer pointing devices
- Reading systems
- Text-to-speech devices
- Voice recognition technology
- Word prediction systems
- Note-taking services
- Signing interpretation services

## E) Eligibility & how to apply for SEN Fund

To seek assistance for the Assistive Technology devices/services, students with special needs who meet the following criteria can obtain a copy of the application form from their respective College LAO:

- The student must be a Singapore Citizen;
- The student is a full-time student in ITE, or has a confirmed place in ITE; and
- The student must have declared his/her SEN condition(s) to the College, with a statement of diagnosis of condition(s) from relevant medical professionals (such as audiologists, physiotherapists, occupational therapists).

The completed form must be submitted to the College LAO together with a statement of diagnosis by relevant medical professionals. Students with special needs can approach the College LAO to find out more information about the SEN Fund.

## F) Getting around in ITE

ITE’s College buildings and infrastructure support the needs of physically-impaired individuals, such as wheelchair users. Examples of barrier-free facilities in ITE Colleges include:

- Access to lifts at every level
- Accessible parking lots for persons with disabilities
- Braille numbers and characters on lift buttons
- Inter-connectivity between buildings that allow for seamless movement
- Washrooms for persons with disabilities

Students with special needs who require additional assistance for access to specific facilities can approach the College LAO to find out more.

## G) Special access arrangements during assessments

Special access arrangements may be made for students with special needs to assess their knowledge and skills competence. Such arrangements would allow them to participate in assessments on an equal basis with their peers.Examples of access arrangements that may be considered include the following:

- Adjustments to assessment settings (e.g. preferential seating)
- Adjustments to assessment timing (e.g. extended time, frequent breaks)
- Adjustments to presentation methods (e.g. large-print, alternative colors)
- Adjustments to response formats (e.g. written, multiple-choice questions)
- Use of Assistive Technology devices

How to apply for special access arrangement

Students with special needs may request for special access arrangements to be made for their assessments. All requests should be supported by relevant documentary evidence such as medical reports, statement of diagnosis, psycho-education assessments from audiologists, physiotherapists, occupational therapists or relevant medical professionals. You may contact your Class Advisor or Manager within the first two weeks of your first semester to seek approval for any special access arrangements required.

## H) Contact us

For advice, guidance or enquiries on learning accessibility and support in ITE, please contact the following:Operating hours are Mon - Fri, 8.30am - 6pm. Closed on weekends and public holidays.

- **ITE College Central**Learning Accessibility OfficeStudent Care @ CentralE-mail: [whatsup@ite.edu.sg](mailto:whatsup@ite.edu.sg) Tel: 8182-7371
- **ITE College East**Learning Accessibility OfficeStudent Care DepartmentE-mail:  [ce.studentcare@ite.edu.sg](mailto:ce.studentcare@ite.edu.sg) Tel: 6544-9287
- **ITE College West**Learning Accessibility OfficeStudent Care DepartmentE-mail:  [cw.studentcare@ite.edu.sg](mailto:cw.studentcare@ite.edu.sg) Tel: 6590-2628
- **Enquiries on Learning Accessibility @ ITE**E-mail:  [edusupport@ite.edu.sg](mailto:edusupport@ite.edu.sg) Tel: 6590-2563

# Student Welfare Officers (SWO)

Our Student Welfare Officers are here to walk with you through various challenges and connect you to the right support.

Last updated 30 April 2026

## Social Work Services

We understand that life can get overwhelming at times, from managing academic pressure and finances to handling personal or family issues. Our Student Welfare Officers are here to walk with you through these challenges and connect you to the right support.

We provide a safe, confidential space for you to talk things through and receive guidance that is practical, respectful, and empowering.

**We support students with:**

- Personal or family-related stress (e.g. conflict, breakdown, grief)
- Mental health or emotional well-being concerns
- Financial difficulties or housing issues
- Risk of school disengagement or dropout
- Navigating complex situations such as abuse, neglect, or crisis
- Referrals to government and community resources (e.g. FSCs, MSF, SSOs, ComLink)

Our Student Welfare Officers work closely with campus staff and external agencies to ensure you get holistic, timely support.

## Contact us

You don’t have to go through it alone. Whether you're looking for someone to talk to or need help figuring out your next step, we’re here to help.

Our operating hours are Mon - Fri, 8.30am – 5.30pm. Closed on weekends and public holidays.

# Types of assessment

At ITE, each course is made up of different modules. There are in-module assessments and end-of-module examinations.

Last updated 9 January 2026

## In-module assessments

The number of in-module assessments you will have to take is different for each module. Examples of in-module assessments include:

- Written tests and assignments
- Practical tests and assignments
- Project

To successfully complete each module, you will need to pass the critical skills required.

## End-of-module examinations

End-of-module examinations test how well you can integrate the various knowledge and skills covered in the module. Examples of end-of-module examinations include:

- Written examinations
- Practical examinations

**Higher Nitec and Nitec (From Jun 26 Exam Series)**

There is no attendance requirement to sit for the end-of-module examination. Students who do not achieve 75% attendance rate for a module and passed the module will have their module grade capped at Grade C.

**Higher Nitec and Nitec in Services/Technology**

There is no attendance requirement to sit for the end-of-module examination. Students who do not achieve 50% attendance rate for a module and passed the module will be awarded a  [Non-Graded Pass](/current-full-time-students/admissions/assessments/grading-system-and-grade-point-average--gpa/higher-nitec-and-nitec-in-services--technology/) .

# Grading system and Grade Point Average (GPA)

GPA represents your current standing in the programme of study. It is the ratio of the total grade points earned to total credits attempted to date. The final GPA score at the point of graduation determines your overall programme performance.

Last updated 4 September 2025

## Grading system

Click on the links below for information of the respective courses:

[Work-Study Diploma (WSDip Grading System)](/current-full-time-students/admissions/assessments/grading-system-and-grade-point-average--gpa/work-study-diploma/)  [Higher Nitec and Nitec](/current-full-time-students/admissions/assessments/grading-system-and-grade-point-average--gpa/higher-nitec-and-nitec/)  [ITE Skills Certificate (ISC)](/current-full-time-students/admissions/assessments/grading-system-and-grade-point-average--gpa/ite-skills-certificate--isc-/)  [Higher Nitec and Nitec in Services / Technology](/current-full-time-students/admissions/assessments/grading-system-and-grade-point-average--gpa/higher-nitec-and-nitec-in-services--technology/)

## Grade Point Average (GPA)

The Grade Point Average (GPA) represents your current standing in the programme of study. It is the ratio of the total grade points earned to total credits attempted to date. The final GPA score at the point of graduation determines your overall programme performance.

The GPA includes all graded modules that are accountable for certification and excludes the following:

- Modules assessed on **Distinction**/**Pass/Fail, Pass/Fail** and **Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory** grading systems
- Exempted modules

# Exam regulations

There are rules and regulations for our examinations. All candidates taking examinations of the Institute of Technical Education (ITE) must comply with the following rules. Candidates who fail to observe any of these rules may be disqualified from the examinations.

Last updated 3 September 2025

Unsure about what is required of you during the examinations?

There are rules and regulations for our examinations. Scroll down to look in details on what to do before, during and after examinations, what to do being hospitalised or faced with MRT train disruptions during examinations, and how to apply for deferment for examinations.

All candidates taking examinations of the Institute of Technical Education (ITE) must comply with the following rules. Candidates who fail to observe any of these rules may be disqualified from the examinations.

## Examination Schedule

1. Candidates are responsible for presenting themselves for examination on the date and time shown in My Exam Schedule via myITE Mobile app or portal ( [https://myite.ite.edu.sg](https://login.microsoftonline.com/13b42c8c-cbcf-4e3d-9d20-f55b7b5ee3c1/saml2?SAMLRequest=fZLNTuswEIVfxZp9EsdpbxurKeq9CIEEoiKBxd05zqQ1SuzicSp4e0J%2FBGy68GLkM%2FPZ58zi6r3v2B49GWcLSGMODK12jbGbAp6rm2gOV8sFqb4TO7kawtY%2B4duAFNjYaEkebwoYvJVOkSFpVY8kg5bl6uFeipjLnXfBadcBWxGhDyPqn7M09OhL9Huj8fnpvoBtCDuSSdJ%2FmIDx18FmiGmTfDGSsnwEdj2CjVXh8NizvnMbY%2BPeaO%2FItcHZzliMteuTNKsnQs91pGvdRhPMmihvBI%2Fa6bSe1VPETKeH6QLYjfMaDx8soFUdIbC76wLURLcG2zw3E9HO5q%2BvvP2TbvPG1LWZm1FDa0Vk9vjdRTTgnaWgbChAcDGNeB7xrOJC8kzyWZym%2FD%2Bw9cmVv8Ye3b5kYX0UkbytqnW0fiwrYC%2Fn1EYBnDKSB7r%2FGc7lweqcCCwv%2B99jUI0KapH8BC1P5e%2FdWH4C&SigAlg=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2F09%2Fxmldsig%23rsa-sha1&Signature=m%2FMVDrD6ytHhipsj4xcBnJGTcB3tBv4Dp9%2BwZM2EAlGzF0qTvHpSECh3Ly%2F7qHbS06o7b%2F3wj3E7FXYZOJHXTW%2FFoXQqQJwWirGP2B1o2301%2Fvx9sJal%2BRNeWgKxtCPEGF%2BRUmiqLs8kho1sgvJkphGM6pAxOKtXauU4BZa6EqrSg9RFbOeZ%2FsNImdAv2RFexyi2Ttnl2lbET96%2FrKiEfgQC%2FVGlkFan%2BhF4WEXfKhqYxZzeq1feuujXNu7nR4Z0T3IoBxDaVSh7j129CLCvBD%2B%2BFpfyQD8Z3OWIhhP9U1nVCPF5NDhUTSdwZ7BajIjurb9TC29b4sSmaJqWSC%2F0ZPv0VPjLuTDvHoAGl3%2BZGJTY2cMgak%2BlhIv2iwRczAS2P3pce1Uvt6RDsibkYYwBKhcnrbrzuEHEwRbtrMYZy0e33qYZDHgjY2NRtTLZ0TeFEJjozAR0JvNpBRWU932qo4BEQWKRW8vxz0tAJwVGoDvTbQuqaeJW3E991QHHLUI6q4A%2F2Z3AdXY9QkALLJYNVSO%2Fl1fqYTHyb8HlUv8L4%2FwZY9nsnJcuflVu4ZY6KaEZbrnve2pMTSdzOxlXMEqvUE%2Ft1%2ByDE9fjOvD5IIW%2BRIf6SMxJ6DYFhNHaeXixPOUrYzXNPL8tGmgp7wn1avzG9UtJm6kidFMIgrZSDstmYIU%3D) ) under the “iStudent” icon. Part-timecandidates can access the exam schedule in My Course via Student Record from Skills Training & Enhancement Portal (STEP) Student Portal. Candidates should report at least 20 minutes before the examination time.

## Before Examination Day (computer-based examination)

1. Candidates should access the online practice examination via myITE to familiarise with taking computer-based examination1.
2. Computer-based examination is accessed through myITE. Candidates should ensure correct password is used to access myITE. Otherwise, candidates may lose time to reset password.

## Before Start of the Examination

1. Only candidates who are registered for the examination are permitted to enter the examination venue.
2. Candidates must bring their photo ID (e.g. physical or digital NRIC/Work Pass/Student Pass; or ITE Student EZ-Link Card) for identification. International candidates whose Student Pass or Work Pass has expired before the examination can seek approval from their Manager of Course to use Passport for identification instead. The candidates must still write or shade their Student ID on the answer scripts/practical works.
3. Candidates are to place their physical photo ID on their desk before commencement of the examination for verification by Invigilator. If the identity of the candidate is in doubt, Invigilator may take a photograph of the candidate for separate verification. Candidates using their digital IC in the SingPass app via their mobile device should unmask their NRIC No./FIN for verification and attendance taking by Invigilator before they are allowed to enter the examination venue.
4. Candidates will be asked to leave the examination venue if their identification documents do not belong to them.
5. Candidates must be properly attired when they turn up for the examination. Full-time candidates are required to be in their College uniform when sitting for the examination in their College. Otherwise, they may be barred from the examination.
6. Candidates are not permitted to eat, drink or smoke in the examination venue.
7. Candidates taking computer-based examinations should also refer to 'Additional Instructions on Computer-based Examinations' and pay attention to the additional instructions announced by the Presiding Examiner or Invigilator at the examination venue before commencement of examination.
8. Candidates are not allowed to bring instruction manuals, external storage media and other peripherals into the examination venue. They are not allowed to possess books, documents, pictures, notes or any unauthorised materials other than those provided by the Presiding Examiner or Invigilator.
9. Open book examinations/tests2

- Candidates are allowed to bring printed and written materials into the examination venue.
10. Electronic and communication devices (e.g. mobile phones, cameras, tablets, smart wrist watches/glasses, pen with image capturing capabilities, ear or headphones etc.) that can display and/or transmit visual or audio information are also not allowed. Any candidates found to be in possession of such materials and devices shall be considered as attempting to cheat and liable to the same penalty as those detected for dishonesty during examinations. If communication devices are left at the front or back of the hall/room, they must be switched off. ITE will not be responsible for any loss of personal belongings
11. Candidates are permitted only to use only non-programmable electronic calculators that are silent. Calculators that give out sound, need external power supply or transmit signals are strictly prohibited. Calculators must not be used for the retrieval of stored data, text or instructions or for the graphical representation of functions and data. Candidates should refer to the guidelines on the features of calculators that are not permitted for use in ITE examinations.
12. **Paper-based Examination**3

1. Candidates are given about 10 minutes before the scheduled examination start time to read the question paper. Candidates must not start writing until instructed to do so by the Presiding Examiner or Invigilator.
13. **Computer-based Examination**

1. Candidates are given about 10 minutes to read the Administrative Instructions page and Question Paper Instructions displayed on candidate's screen. At the start time of the examination, the system will allow candidates to begin the examination.
14. Candidates must inform the Presiding Examiner or Invigilator immediately if they are not issued the correct module question paper or supplementary materials (e.g. formulae sheet).

## During the Examination

1. No candidates are allowed to enter the examination venue after 30 minutes have lapsed from the scheduled start time of the examination.
2. Candidates may leave the examination venue after 30 minutes have lapsed from the start of the examination and they are not allowed to return to the examination venue.
3. Candidates may leave and re-enter the examination venue only if they are accompanied by an Invigilator or a person authorised by the Presiding Examiner.
4. For computer-based examination, the candidate who temporarily leaves the examination venue escorted by an Invigilator must navigate to the Progress Summary page to protect the responses.
5. Open book examinations/tests

- Candidates are not allowed to bring along any of their printed and written materials when they temporarily leave the examination venue.
6. Candidates must not, for any reason, communicate with other candidates during the examination. Candidates shall not do anything which causes unnecessary distraction to other candidates. Candidates who are guilty of improper conduct or misbehaviour may be asked to leave the examination venue.
7. Any candidate who wishes to communicate with an Invigilator must remain seated and raise his/her hand.
8. Candidates are not allowed to borrow stationery and mathematical instruments such as rulers and calculators from other candidates during the examination.
9. Candidates should note that legible handwriting is considered in the award of marks for paper-based examination. Candidates should use black or blue ballpoint pen during the examinations. Candidates are also reminded to use a soft-lead pencil (e.g. 2B) to shade their answers on the Answer Sheet. A soft eraser should be used for erasure if candidates wish to change their answers. It is the responsibility of the candidates to ensure that answers are presented clearly in Answer Sheet / Answer Scripts for marking.
10. Candidates will not be given extra time for printing of responses for submission (if required).
11. Candidates will be stopped from proceeding further in the practical examination if they continue to adopt unsafe or dangerous method of operation despite warning. An unsafe or dangerous method of operation is one which may injure candidates or cause damage to machines or equipment.
12. Candidates are liable for any damage to machines, tools and equipment arising from their negligence.

## At the End of the Examination

1. Candidates who are allowed into the examination venue within 30 minutes after scheduled start time of the examination will not be given extra time at the end of examination.
2. After the first 30 minutes from start of examination, candidates must raise their hand if he/she has completed the examination. Once confirmed by the Invigilator, the candidate can leave the examination venue.
3. **Paper-based examination**

1. No candidates are allowed to leave the examination venue during the last 15 minutes of the examination. This is to facilitate the administration and collection of answer scripts.
2. Candidates should stop writing/working immediately when instructed by the Presiding Examiner or Invigilator.
3. Candidates should remain seated while the answer scripts/practical works are being collected.
4. Candidates should not take question paper, used and unused answer booklets or any items issued by the Invigilator out of the examination venue unless otherwise stated.
5. Open book examinations/tests

- Candidates are allowed to take away only the printed and written materials they have brought into the examination venue.
4. **Computer-based examination**

1. Candidates will have their responses auto submitted if he/she has not submitted at the examination end time.
2. Candidates must **not** exit the application or shut down the PC/notebook.
5. For examinations where more than one relay is carried out, candidates are not allowed to leave until the end of the examination, unless otherwise instructed by the Presiding Examiner or Invigilator.
6. Candidates can leave the examination venue only after they have been told to do so by the Presiding Examiner or Invigilator.

## Academic Dishonesty

1. A candidate is guilty of academic dishonesty if he/she cheats or attempts to cheat during the examination.
2. Candidates found guilty of academic dishonesty will be graded ‘Fail’ and may face disciplinary action.

## Posting of Examination Material Online

1. Candidates are not allowed to post any examination-related material (e.g. whole or part of question(s), question paper, answer script) on any social media or web page. Candidates found doing so will be subjected to disciplinary action.

## Deferment of Examination

1. Candidates who are unable to sit for examination but have a valid reason can seek for deferment to the next examination series. Candidates are to submit their request to their Manager of Course for approval before the date of examination.
2. For reason of absence which cannot be known beforehand, candidates must submit their applications with supporting documents within the **next two working days** from the date of examination. The supporting documents (including digital documents) should be the original copy. In cases where the supporting document is required by more than one party (e.g. medical claim and proof of absence), photocopy of the supporting document can be accepted. However, the photocopy must be certified as true copy by ITE staff who are designated as Lecturers and above after original copy is sighted.

## Absence from Examination

1. Candidates who are absent from an end-of-module examination without ITE’s approval will be considered to have failed the module.

## Infectious Diseases and Hospitalised Candidates

1. Candidates who are suffering from any infectious disease (e.g. chicken pox) are **not allowed**to sit for examination at the assigned examination venue. Arrangement for a hospitalised candidate to sit for examination will be considered on case-by-case basis. For SARS, H1N1, COVID-19 or any other infectious diseases advised by MOH, additional instructions will be issued where necessary for compliance.

## Major Train Service Disruption

1. In the event of major train service disruption, candidates should still make their way to the examination venue. Candidates may be allowed to take examinations with full duration given if they arrive before the end of the examination and provided no other candidates have left the examination venue. Otherwise, candidates may be allowed to take make-up examinations.

*¹ Computer-based examination refers to examinations conducted in ITE Integrated Assessment System (IAS).*

*² ‘Open book’ is printed on the cover page of question papers.*

*3**Paper-based examination refers to both written and practical examination.*

# Release of module results

Find out how you can view your ITE module results.

Last updated 26 January 2026

## Important dates to note

Please visit  [Important dates to note](/current-full-time-students/admissions/assessments/important-dates-to-note/)  page for:

- Release date of module results
- Closing date for application of review of module results
- Upload of Digital certificates/academic transcripts to MySkillsFuture Careers & Skills Passport
- Collection Period for certificates / academic transcripts for graduates

## Viewing your module results

When your module results are released, you can view your results by logging in to the ITE myPortal site:

- **Full-time & Traineeship:** myITE → iStudent → Student Center → Academic Records → View My Grades
- **Part-time:** STEP Student Portal → Academic Advisement

## Certificate, Academic Transcript & Statement of Results

**Full-time Work-Study Diploma, Higher Nitec and Nitec**

An e-Statement of Results (e-SOR) can be generated by clicking on 'View Statement of Results (eSOR)' in the View My Grades page. The e-SOR will show the grades and credits earned in all the modules that you have taken, together with your Grade Point Average (GPA).

**Part-time****Higher Nitec and Nitec in Services / Technology**

Your e-Statement of Results (e-SOR), e-Module Certificate and e-Modular Skills Certificate will be accessible from your STEP Student Portal. The e-SOR/e-Module Certificate will show the grade earned for the module that you have taken. The e-Modular Skills Certificate will show the grades for 2 to 4 bite-sized modules that you have completed.

### Note:

If you have successfully completed your course, you will be provided with the date for the collection of your certificate and academic transcript. Certificates and academic transcripts can be collected at the specified ITE Graduation Ceremony. Your digital certificate and academic transcript will be accessible from your MySkillsFuture Careers & Skills Passport.

If you are unable to attend the Graduation Ceremony, you can collect the certificate and academic transcript from the ITE Customer & Visitor Centre of the College you studied at, during office hours.

**Hard copy certificates will be issued during the Graduation Ceremony. Certificates that remain uncollected after****one yea****r will be destroyed and cannot be re-issued**.

Visit ITE e-Services for  [Digital Certificates](/current-full-time-students/admissions/assessments/digital-certificates-for-ite-graduates/)  (ITE graduates)

## Review of module results

You may request to review your module results if you have reasons to believe that the module grade awarded for a particular module should have been better. Request should be submitted with a payment of $20 per module.

**Full-time Higher Nitec, Nitec, Technical Diploma & Technical Engineering Diploma; and Work-Study Diploma**

You may request for review of module results by submitting the online form  [here](https://form.gov.sg/68958dd0592624a910aa1bbd) , before 5.30pm on the closing date.

You will be informed by email of ITE's decision on the review of the module results.

**Part-time Higher Nitec and Nitec****in Services / Technology**

You may request for review of module results by logging in to the STEP Student Portal  [here](https://stms.polite.edu.sg/) , and submit the request before the closing date. You can raise a 'Grade review' request under "Request & task" panel.

### Note:

If the review leads to a change in grade, your payment will be refunded. ITE’s decision on the review is final.

If you have failed a module, you will be required to repeat the module.

# Digital certificates for ITE Graduates

Full-time, Traineeship and Part-time College students who graduated from ITE are able to access digital copy of their certificates and transcripts in their MySkillsFuture Careers & Skills Passport.

Last updated 4 September 2025

Full-time, Traineeship and Part-time College students who graduated from ITE are able to access digital copy of their certificate in their MySkillsFuture Careers & Skills Passport

Availability of certificate for ITE graduates

| Certification | Graduates |
| --- | --- |
| Higher Nitec/Nitec | From May 2002 exam series onwards |
| Work-Study Diploma | From September 2020 exam series onwards |
| ITE Skills Certificate (ISC) | From June 2021 exam series onwards |
| ITE Skills Subject Certificate (ISSC) | From October 2022 exam series onwards |
| ITE-Partner Joint Diploma | From December 2024 exam series onwards |

The digital certificates are secured by blockchain technology which can be viewed, checked and verified on the OpenCerts platform developed by GovTech Singapore.

**Benefits**

- Share qualification credentials to potential employers and educational institutions that negate the need for verification.
- Common platform removing the hassle of moving in between different platforms when verifying certificates.
- Accessed anytime and anywhere

## Step-by-step guide for ITE Graduates

**Step 1**

- You may retrieve your Digital Certificate issued by ITE by logging in to MySkillsFuture Careers &Skills Passport with SingPass.
- For any assistance needed, please refer to  [Careers & Skills Passport](https://www.myskillsfuture.gov.sg/csp) .

**Step 2**

- Verify the certificate by dropping the OpenCerts file on the [Open Certs website](https://opencerts.io/) . Please use Chrome Browser to watch the video guide below:

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

**What is OpenCerts Blockchain platform?**

OpenCerts is the umbrella trademark and the platform is backed by the Ethereum blockchain technology to generate crytographic protections for educational credentials issued by legitimate institutions. ITE is one of the legitimate issuing institutions on the OpenCerts platform.

**Can I rename my OpenCerts file?**

You may rename your OpenCerts file but you must retain the file extension (.opencert).

**Can I use any internet browser to view the OpenCerts website?**

The OpenCerts website is best viewed using Chrome Browser.

# Academic awards

Learn about ITE’s Certificate of Merit, Diploma with Merit, and Course Medals awarded to top-performing graduates with outstanding results.

Last updated 27 August 2025

## Certificate of Merit (COM) / Diploma with Merit (DWM)

- Certificate of Merit (COM) is generally awarded to the top 5% of the graduates from each *Higher Nitec*and *Nitec*course.
- Diploma with Merit (DWM) is generally awarded to the top 8% of the graduates from each Work-Study Diploma course.
- Graduates must have passed all core modules at the first attempt within normal course duration and have achieved outstanding performance in their course of study, with a cumulative GPA of 3.5 or above, at the point of graduation, to be considered for the award of COM/DWM.

## Course Medals

- Course Medals are awarded to the outstanding COM / DWM holders in each course. The number of Course Medals awarded for each course is based on the number of graduates in the course, subject to a maximum of 3 medals.
- Graduates will be awarded Gold, Silver or Bronze Course Medals based on their overall performance in their course of study, CCA achievements and other contributions.

# Application for Certified Statement, Statement of Results, Academic Transcript

ITE graduates may apply for a Certified Statement, copy of Statement of Results, or Academic Transcript via e-application or at any ITE Customer & Visitor Centre during office hours.

Last updated 23 September 2025

ITE does not issue duplicate copies of a certificate.

If you are an ITE graduate issued with the Digital Certificate and Transcripts, you can retrieve your Digital Certificate and Transcript by logging into MySkillsFuture  [Careers & Skills Passport](https://www.myskillsfuture.gov.sg/content/portal/en/index.html)  with your Singpass ( [click](https://www.ite.edu.sg/current-full-time-students/admissions/assessments/digital-certificates-for-ite-graduates/)  to view the List of ITE certifications issued with Digital Certificate and Transcripts).

If you are not issued with a Digital Certificate and Transcripts, you can apply for a Certified Statement or a copy of the Statement of Results, or Academic Transcript using the form  [here](https://form.gov.sg/689598575ba5d914ddca3ceb)  or at any of the ITE Customer & Visitor Centres during office hours.

There is an administrative fee of $10 per course per type of statement and the processing and delivery by post of the statement(s) applied may take up to one week.

# Learner experience

At ITE, we design our curriculum and programmes with our students in mind. Discover ITE’s unique ‘Hands-on, Minds-on, Hearts-on™’ education.

Last updated 27 August 2025

If you learn best by doing and experiencing, our unique 'Hands-on, Minds-on, Hearts-on'™ education is the way to go for you! We have a nurturing environment and caring lecturers to help you rediscover the joy of learning.

## Unique ‘Hands-on, Minds-on, Hearts-on™’ College Education

Our holistic education aims to give you an all-round development through:

- ***Hands-on***training to equip you with employable skill sets
- ***Minds-on***learning to develop you into an independent-thinking and highly adaptable individual
- ***Hearts-on***learning to nurture you into a person who has passion for what you do, has self-belief and who cares for the community and society

As an ITE student, you’ll get to practise what you have learnt. We integrate theory with practice through coursework, industry exposure, projects and experiential learning. Our aim is for you to become an all-rounded ***'Career-Ready****,****Life-Ready and World-Ready'***graduate.

## Real world, Real work learning

Nothing beats learning from real life professionals. ITE’s courses are designed, in close consultation with industry, to ensure that you are equipped with work-ready skills relevant to changing industry needs when you graduate.

Industry internship is a key part of our technical education. You’ll spend three to six months in industry to gain valuable real work experience and important life skills through the Enhanced Internship Programme under the **'Campus@Workplace'**approach. Our Lecturers will be constantly in touch with you, to ensure the success of your internship experience.

We work with industry to create authentic learning environments and facilities to mimic the ‘real world’ future workplace within our Colleges. Through collaboration with industry partners, we have set up various learning facilities like the **Healthcare Simulation Training Centre@College East**, **Amber | West Training Restaurant**, and **Aerospace Hub@College Central**. To make learning more engaging, we have introduced innovative ways of teaching and learning, through immersive **AR and VR technology** to simulate authentic industry environment that is difficult to physically simulate within campuses (e.g. offshore oil rig platform, aircraft/airport) . This is what we call our **‘Workplace@Campus’** learning approach.

## Student life – It’s not all work and no play!

You’ll also enjoy a comprehensive range of learning facilities, such as high-tech learning spaces and digital learning approaches in our modern workshops and laboratories.

For amenities, we provide sports and recreational centres (gym, stadium and swimming pools), and performing arts studios and theatres.

Want to meet like-minded schoolmates and explore avenues to showcase your interests and talents? Take your pick from more than 100 Co-Curricular Activities available to enrich your life as a full-time student at ITE.

## The learning never stops

Started work and keen to upgrade your skills? In line with national SkillsFuture initiatives, ITE is committed to providing quality Continuing Education and Training (CET) courses to help equip you for life. CET learning options are delivered in an **A.B.C. format –*****Accessible, Bite-size****and****Convenient***, with classes conducted at night or during weekends to provide convenience to learners.

There are also recognised **Work-Study Diploma** programmes for ITE graduates and in-service workers with prerequisite skills. Our diploma graduates can look forward to applying to a related full-time or part-time degree programme at the National University of Singapore, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore Institute of Technology and Singapore University of Social Sciences, subject to the admission requirements of the Universities.

Life @ ITE – It’s Truly Exciting!

# ITE Graduation 2026

Heartiest congratulations to the Class of 2026!

Last updated 9 July 2026

Every year, we hold the graduation ceremony to honour your hard work and achievements. It is a day to celebrate with your family and friends, making it a truly special occasion. This event is all about recognising your success and marking an important milestone in your life.

Graduation is not just about the ceremony; it is a chance to remember the amazing experiences you have had with us. Think back on the fun times, friendships, and learning moments that have shaped your journey. Together, we celebrate your growth and the unforgettable memories you have created.

**ITE Graduation 2026****Wednesday 22 July 2026****2.30 pm****Tay Eng Soon Convention Centre (Blk A, Level 4)**

ITE Headquarters & ITE College Central2 Ang Mo Kio DriveSingapore 567720Click  [here](/about-ite/colleges/college-central/locate-us/)  to view map of ITE Headquarters and ITE College Central.

A confirmation email with the event details will be sent **by Friday 10 July 2026**, to those who have RSVP’d “Yes”.

If you have RSVP’d “Yes” and have not received the confirmation email by then, please write to  [admissions_csp@ite.edu.sg](mailto:admissions_csp@ite.edu.sg)  for assistance.

# Message by CEO

For Class of 2026

Last updated 7 July 2026

**Dear Graduands,**

On behalf of the Institute of Technical Education (ITE), congratulations on completing your studies. You are among **10,955** graduands from ITE's Full-time, Part-time, Traineeship and Work-Study programmes for Academic Year 2025/2026 — and each of you has earned this moment through your dedication, resilience and hard work.

Your graduation is a significant milestone. Each of you has taken a different path to reach this moment. Some chose ITE as the first step into post-secondary education, drawn by our wide range of courses and driven by a clear sense of what you wanted to pursue. Others came after going through life challenges, determined to discover and develop your potential. Some came with years of work experience to upgrade and stay relevant. Whatever your starting point, ITE believed in you — and today, your success affirms that belief.

You graduate at a time of rapid change, but also great opportunity. During your time at ITE, you have gained not only technical competencies, but also the values, work ethic, and adaptability that employers seek and that life demands. Employers have affirmed that our students contribute meaningfully at work, with strong practical skills, positive attitudes, and readiness for the workplace. That is a reflection of who you are. You leave ITE not just job-ready, but future-ready.

Your journey does not end here — it is just beginning. With a wide range of progression opportunities, including Technical Diploma and Work-Study Diploma courses at ITE, as well as Diploma courses at Polytechnics, there is always a pathway to help you grow further. As your career develops and the landscape evolves, the willingness to stay curious and keep learning will be key to your long-term success. ITE will always be your partner in this lifelong journey, with Continuing Education and Training programmes to help you build your skills and qualifications.

As alumni, you also have a vital role to play.  I encourage you to stay connected with the ITE family, and we look forward to having you working alongside ITE as mentors, supervisors in the workplace or even as lecturers in ITE to inspire the next generation of our students, just as others have inspired you.

I wish you every success and happiness in the years ahead and look forward to seeing you become the skilled and resilient professionals that Singapore needs.

Congratulations, Class of AY2025-2026!

**Peter Lam**Chief Executive OfficerInstitute of Technical Education

# Important Information

Find out essential details for ITE Graduation 2026!

Last updated 2 July 2026

**ITE Graduation 2026****Wednesday 22 July 2026****2.30 pm****Tay Eng Soon Convention Centre (Blk A, Level 4)**

ITE Headquarters & ITE College Central2 Ang Mo Kio DriveSingapore 567720Click  [here](/about-ite/colleges/college-central/locate-us/)  to view map of ITE Headquarters and ITE College Central.

**Important Details**

Only graduands who have registered their attendance online for the ITE Graduation 2026 by Friday 19 June 2026 *[extended]* will:

- Receive a Confirmation email with further details about the ceremony by Friday 10 July 2026; and

- Secure a reserved seat in the Auditorium, based on the presentation sequence on stage.

*Please note**:*- G*raduands who arrive late, after the close of event day registration, will not be presented on stage.**- Graduands who have indicated ‘Not Attending’ in the online registration form or who did not register their attendance online by Fri 19 Jun 2026 [extended] will not have seats reserved for them and will not be presented on stage.*

## Graduation Gown

Graduands attending the ITE Graduation 2026 are required to wear the ITE Graduation Gown. Graduands are advised to dress neatly and appropriately for the occasion. See  [Dress Code](/current-full-time-students/life-at-ite/ite-graduation/information-on-dress-code/) .

*Note: Graduands currently serving National Service are allowed to be presented on stage in full military uniform (including cap/beret). The graduation gown should not be worn over the military uniform.*

For further information regarding the rental or purchase of the ITE Graduation Gown, please click  [here](https://www.myuniformshop.com.sg/ite-graduation) .

## Items to bring on Ceremony Day

- Print the Confirmation Email (with barcode) or display the barcode on phone
- ITE Graduation Gown

** Please refrain from bringing big or bulky bags.*

## Useful Information

**1. Invited guests (limited to 2 guests only)**

- Admission into the Auditorium is strictly by registration only.
- The seating capacity in the Auditorium at Tay Eng Soon Convention Centre is limited.
- Seating for Guests is on a first come, first served basis.
- In the event that all seats in the Auditorium are filled, guests will be ushered to the Function Hall (located opposite the Auditorium) to watch the graduation ceremony via live streaming.
- Guests may proceed to the Auditorium to be seated from 1.30 pm. Guests are requested to be seated by 2.15 pm. (Graduands are to be seated by 2.05 pm.)
- Out of courtesy to other guests,

- Guests’ mobile phones must be switched to silent mode inside the auditorium.
- Children below the age of six will not be admitted into the Auditorium.
- Guests should not leave the auditorium until the entire ceremony is over. Do note that walk-ins or unregistered guests will not be accepted.

**2. Carpark information**

There are limited parking lots at ITE Headquarters & ITE College Central. If guests are driving to the venue, please park at the nearby HDB carparks.

**3. Photo taking**

- Professional photographers will be present to take photos on stage. Please advise guests to refrain from taking photos during the graduation ceremony.
- Photographs will be available for download and details will be emailed to graduands after the event.
- Photos and videos will be taken at this event, which may be used in various communications platforms, including but not limited to publications, ITE website and social media platforms.

**4. Contact details**

For further clarification on ITE Graduation 2026, please email to  [admissions_csp@ite.edu.sg](mailto:admissions_csp@ite.edu.sg) .

# Top Graduate Awards

Read more about our top graduate awards and the winners!

Last updated 29 May 2026

## Lee Kuan Yew Gold Medal

The Lee Kuan Yew Awards for ITE students were instituted in 1999 through the sale proceeds of the special edition of "The Singapore Story" memoirs by Singapore’s first Prime Minister, Mr Lee Kuan Yew. A sum of $555,000 was donated to ITE for the establishment of the awards.The Lee Kuan Yew Gold Medals for ITE students are aimed at promoting technical education by giving greater recognition to the achievements of ITE students and trainees.Lee Kuan Yew Gold Medals are awarded to the top graduates from ITE College Central, ITE College East and ITE College West, who have excelled in their course of study and co-curricular activities, and made contributions to an enriching College life.

## Tay Eng Soon Gold Medal

The Tay Eng Soon Scholarship Fund was established in November 1993, in honour of the late Dr Tay Eng Soon. Dr Tay Eng Soon was the Minister-in-Charge of technical and polytechnic education from 1981 to 1993, and the Chairman of ITE (and the former Vocational & Industrial Training Board). One of the objectives of the Fund is to provide medals and/or prizes to ITE students.

Tay Eng Soon Gold Medals are awarded to the top graduates from ITE College Central, ITE College East and ITE College West, who have achieved excellent course performance, participated actively in co-curricular activities and contributed to the well-being and development of their College.

## The Ngee Ann Kongsi Gold Medal

The Ngee Ann Kongsi Gold Medals are awarded to the top graduates from ITE College Central, ITE College East and ITE College West, for their outstanding course performance, active participation in co-curricular activities and contributions to the Colleges. The gold medals, first presented in 2018, are funded by The Ngee Ann Kongsi, a non-profit Teochew philanthropic foundation actively involved in educational, cultural and charitable activities in Singapore. Over the years, the Kongsi has made significant contributions towards the enrichment of Singapore society and its education scene.

## Singapore National Employers Federation Gold Medal

The Singapore National Employers Federation Gold Medals are awarded to top performing graduates of the Work-Study Diploma Programme who have excelled in their course of study and have made contributions to the workplace training, company’s projects and activities. The Singapore National Employers Federation Gold Medals are sponsored by the Singapore National Employers Federation (SNEF).

## Singapore Business Federation Gold Medal

The Singapore Business Federation Gold Medal is awarded to the top graduate of the Technical Engineer Diploma / Technical Diploma Programme for outstanding course performance. The Singapore Business Federation Gold Medal is sponsored by the Singapore Business Federation (SBF).

## Singapore Precision Engineering & Technology Association Gold Medal

The Singapore Precision Engineering & Technology Association Gold Medal is awarded to a top performing graduate of the Work-Study Diploma Programme (Engineering/IT-related), working in the manufacturing industry and has made outstanding contributions at the workplace.The SPETA Gold Medal is sponsored by the Singapore Precision Engineering & Technology Association (SPETA).

## e2i Gold Medal

The objectives of the e2i Gold Medal are to promote lifelong learning among adult learners to increase their employability, and to motivate and give recognition to Continuing Education & Training (CET) graduates for their upgrading efforts and achievements.The e2i Gold Medal is sponsored by e2i (Employment and Employability Institute), which helps working people grow their skills and career through career coaching, developing better skills and job matching.

## IES Engineering Award

The IES Engineering Award is awarded to a top ITE graduate for outstanding performance in an Engineering course and contributions in Engineering-related projects and activities. The IES Engineering Award is sponsored by the Institution of Engineers, Singapore.

## ITE-SkillsFuture Lifelong Learning Award

The ITE-SkillsFuture Lifelong Learning Award recognises exemplary graduates of Work-Study Diploma Programme who have made significant efforts in their lifelong learning journey and created positive impact by fostering a culture of continuous learning within their workplace or immediate social network, all while effectively managing their professional and personal responsibilities.

## ITE Outstanding Progress Award

The ITE Outstanding Progress Awards are awarded to exemplary graduates from ITE College Central, ITE College East and ITE College West, who have shown strong perseverance in overcoming challenges to complete their course, displayed exemplary conduct, and made valuable contributions to their College and community.

## Tay Eng Soon Scholarship (TESS)

Tay Eng Soon Scholarships are presented to outstanding ITE graduates who have performed well academically and attained good co-curricular activity records. The TESS is open to ITE graduates pursuing a full-time Diploma course in ITE or the polytechnics. Selection for this award is based on merit.

## Graduation Matters

Table 1: Frequently Asked Questions on Graduation Matters

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |

| I am unable to attend the graduation ceremony, can I still collect my award? | Graduands, who are unable to attend the graduation ceremony, will be informed via email on the collection of the certificate/medal at a later date, after the graduation ceremony. |
| Is it compulsory to attend the graduation ceremony? | Invited graduands are encouraged to attend the graduation ceremony as it is to recognize their outstanding performance.Clickherefor details on ITE Graduation 2026. |
| Why is children below the age of six not allowed in the auditorium? | For safety and comfort reasons, children under the age of six are not permitted in the auditorium during the graduation ceremony.However, guests with children under the age of six may still view the ceremony via the screening in the hall. |
