# Centre for Music and the Arts (CEMTA)

The Centre for Music and The Arts (CeMTA) aims to promote student activities both in the performing and visual arts across ITE Colleges.

Last updated 19 November 2025

## About ITE Centre for Music and the Arts (CeMTA)

ITE Centre for Music and the Arts (CeMTA) welcomes students from all three ITE Colleges to nurture their passion for music, drama and dance. Our mission is to empower our students with skills and values that will prepare them for their future careers, leveraging their artistic talents.

CeMTA plays a vital role in shaping our students’ character through our diverse arts and leadership programmes. Our five performance CCA groups –  [ITE Concert Band](https://www.instagram.com/iteconcertband) ,  [ITE Modern Dance](https://www.instagram.com/itemoderndance) ,  [ITE Show Choir](https://www.instagram.com/ite.showchoir) ,  [ITE That Acappella Group (TAG)](https://www.instagram.com/itethatacappellagroup)  and  [ITE Theatrical Ensemble](https://www.instagram.com/theatricalensemble/)  – provide a platform for students to develop and shine.

Signature events produced by CeMTA include ITE Vocal Xchange, ITE Singer-Songwriters Showcase, ITE Dance Emblazon, the ITE Musical, Musica Fantasia, as well as Theatrical Ensemble’s presentations: Chapters, Seasons, Volumes and Episodes. CeMTA’s productions are opportunities to collaborate with our valued partners, including ITE courses and industry professionals.

CeMTA students are encouraged to play an active part in giving back to ITE and the community. Our student engagement programme, CeMTAConnect, fosters collaboration and friendships across the five CCA groups and three Colleges.

Connect with us  [@itecemta](https://www.instagram.com/itecemta) .

## ITE Arts Platforms

The signature ITE events organised by CeMTA are holistic development programmes where students learn essential life skills through the Arts. The focus of the productions are on the learning journey rather than the outcome, giving the students the time and space to grow under the tutelage of industry professionals.

Other than performing arts talents, students from related courses and with relevant skills have the opportunity to work on their areas of expertise. Past collaborators include students from:

ITE College Central:

- *Higher Nitec* in Performance Production (School of Design and Media)
- *Nitec*in Visual Communications (School of Design and Media)
- *Higher Nitec* in Filmmaking (Cinematography) (School of Design and Media)
- *Nitec*in Interactive Media Design (School of Design and Media)

ITE College East:

- *Nitec* in Beauty & Wellness (School of Business & Services)
- *Nitec* in Hair Fashion & Design (School of Business & Services)
- *Nitec* in Electrical Technology (Lighting and Sound) (School of Engineering)

## ITE Dance Emblazon

ITE Dance Emblazon is ITE’s annual combined dance concert. Inaugurated in 2013, it brings together more than 300 dance talents from all over ITE in five dance genres, including hip-hop, modern dance, b-boy, Malay Dance and K-pop dance.

Emblazon symbolises the igniting of ITE students’ passion for dance, and displays the capabilities of ITE talents in staging a professional dance performance. The objective of the programmes is to develop “Thinking Dancers”, where dancers are challenged not only to perform, but also to take ownership of various aspects of the production. This includes social media marketing, where students manage updates of the production on Instagram - @itedanceemblazon2024.

**ITE Dance Emblazon 2024 will be held on 27 & 28 September. Ticketing Details here*  [https://sg.bookmyshow.com/events/ite-dance-emblazon-2024/ITEDEB24](https://sg.bookmyshow.com/events/ite-dance-emblazon-2024/ITEDEB24)

## ITE Vocal XChange

ITE’s annual combined vocal concert brings together over 100 vocal talents from all over ITE, embodying the spirit of continuous learning and sharing, where students exchange their learning points and share their singing techniques with each other.

The ITE Vocal XChange aims to encourage a ground-up arts initiative, educating young arts talents not only through the performing experience, but also in technical production and arts management. The production and marketing teams comprise student leaders from various vocal and music groups from the ITE Colleges and CeMTA – ITE Show Choir, ITE That Acappella Group (T.A.G), College East Voices in Paradise, College East Dynamics, College Central’s Central Music Club and West Unplugged. For more info, visit the student-managed Instagram page @itevocalxchange

## ITE Art Show

Held every two years since 2012, the ITE Visual Arts Show has been offering a spectacle of diverse artistic works created by ITE students and staff. More than 300 pieces of art works by students and staff from all three ITE Colleges and community groups are displayed.

The exhibits go beyond the gallery - the art creations spill off the canvases and are displayed throughout the campus. These include Artworks from community arts projects, coursework as well as individual contributions. The bi-annual Art Show rotates among the ITE College.

## ITE Musical

The ITE Musical had its humble beginnings more than 10 years ago, with the first production of *Midsummer’s Night Dream* staged at the Kallang Theatre. It produced one of Singapore’s most prolific theatre actresses, Siti Khalijah Zainal, who was then an ITE student.

Many more Broadway and West End musical adaptations followed – *Joseph and the Amazing Technicolour Dreamcoat (2007), Grease (2009),* *West Side Story (2011)*and *Fame (2013).*In 2015, an original musical, *Becoming Home,* was created to commemorate SG50, including collaborations with community members of different age groups. In 2017*,* CeMTA produced*Letters to ITE* - another original musical - to celebrate ITE’s 25th Anniversary. This production was the biggest so far, involving 200 talented student singers, musicians, dancers and actors from across the ITE Colleges.

## CCAs managed by ITE Centre for Music and the Arts

The CCAs managed by ITE CeMTA consist student members from all colleges, and represent whole of ITE. Currently, the trainings are held at ITE College Central.

- ITE Concert Band (IG: @iteconcertband)
- ITE Modern Dance (IG: @itemoderndance)
- ITE Show Choir (IG: @ite_showchoir)
- ITE That Acappella Group (IG: @itethatacappellagroup)
- ITE Theatrical Ensemble (IG: @itetheatricalensemble)

# Overseas exposure

Last year, we have sent more than 4,000 students abroad, across 25 countries, for short-term exposure. We are continuing to ramp up overseas exposure opportunities as part of our aim to build ‘world-ready’ graduates.

Last updated 11 September 2025

Over the last year, we have sent more than 4,000 students abroad, across 25 countries, for short-term exposure. We are continuing to ramp up overseas exposure opportunities as part of our aim to build ‘world-ready’ graduates. Such exposure can take the following forms:

**Overseas Industrial Attachment Programme** (OIAP), where our students are attached to companies for a short working stint in foreign countries. This helps them to appreciate working in different culture and environment, and enhance their readiness to work overseas upon graduation.

**Overseas Student Exchange Programme** (OSEP), where our students attend classes in overseas institutions and earn credits towards their certifications.

**Overseas Service & Development Programme**(OSDP), where our students undertake community service projects as part of being compassionate global citizens. Our students also take part in overseas competitions, seminars, conferences and leadership programmes to hone their skills, competencies and character.

In addition, we also welcome overseas students from our partner institutions for exchanges in ITE.

# Work-Study Diploma Graduation

Last updated 25 November 2025

Work-Study Diploma Graduation 2025 has concluded. Please check for updates on certificate collection and other post-ceremony details.

### 🎓 Work-Study Diploma Graduation Ceremony 2025

Every year, we come together to celebrate the achievements of our Work-Study Diploma graduands.

The graduation ceremony is a special day to honour your hard work and perseverance, and to share this proud moment with your family, friends, employers, and lecturers.

This is your milestone – a time to look back on your journey with pride and to look forward with confidence.

# Important Information For Graduands

To attend the Work-Study Diploma Graduation Ceremony 2025, please follow these steps:

Last updated 18 May 2026

## 📝 Before the Ceremony

To help you get ready for your big day, here are some important steps:

### 1️⃣ Register Your Attendance

•**Registration Period:** Wed 08 Oct 2025 – Wed 22 Oct 2025 (11:59pm)

•All graduands will receive a unique **invitation email** to RSVP.

•Register your own attendance **and your guests (up to 2 guests only)**.

•You will receive an **Acknowledgement Email** once your registration is submitted.

📩 Didn’t receive the invitation email? Write to  [**rsvp@theevents.tech**](mailto:rsvp@theevents.tech) .

### 2️⃣ Rent or Purchase Your ITE Graduation Gown

•**Rental/Purchase Period:** Wed 15 Oct 2025 – Sat 08 Nov 2025

•All graduands attending the ceremony are required to wear the **ITE Graduation Gown**.

•Graduands in **military uniform** will not be presented on stage. Please change into the recommended outfit before donning the gown.

•[Click  [here](https://www.myuniformshop.com.sg/ite-graduation)  for more details on gown rental/purchase]

•Remember to dress neatly and appropriately for this special occasion.

### 3️⃣ Receive Confirmation Email

•Only graduands who indicated they are attending will receive a **Confirmation Email** with full ceremony details.

•If you do not receive it by **Fri 07 Nov 2025**, please contact  [**rsvp@theevents.tech**](mailto:rsvp@theevents.tech) .

✨ Get ready to celebrate your achievement with pride and joy – we can’t wait to see you there!

## 🎉 On the Day of the Ceremony

Here’s what you need to know to make your graduation day smooth and memorable:

### ✅ What to Bring

•**Important Information Email with QR Code** – either printed or displayed on your mobile (for verification at the registration counter).

•**Your ITE Graduation Gown** – graduands without the gown will not be allowed on stage.

•Please avoid bringing **large or bulky bags**.

### 🕘 Registration of Attendance

•**Morning Session:** 9.00am – 9.50am

•**Afternoon Session:** 2.00pm – 2.50pm

•📍 Location: Registration Counter, outside the Library Foyer (Block A, Level 4)

•Attendance can only be registered using the **QR code** sent to your RSVP confirmation email.

•Ensure your QR code is ready for scanning at the counter.

### Important Notes

•Please be punctual. Registration will close **strictly at 9.50am (Morning) and 2.50pm (Afternoon)**.

•Graduands who arrive late (after registration closes) **will not be registered and cannot go on stage** to receive their certificate/medal.

•Walk-ins or unregistered graduands **will not be allowed** to participate.

✨ Be on time, be prepared, and get ready to celebrate your success in front of your family, friends, and lecturers!

### 🎓 Graduation Gown Robing

•All graduands must be in their **ITE Graduation Gown** before proceeding to the Auditorium.

•Only graduands wearing the official gown will be allowed to join the proceedings.

•Graduands in **military uniform** will not be presented on stage. Please change into the recommended attire before donning the gown.

•**Gown rental/purchase** will also be available on the day of the ceremony. The vendor’s counter will be at **Room K423**, open from **8.30am – 10am** (AM session); and **1.30pm – 3pm** (PM session).

•A **robing area** will be provided. Please follow the directional signs and put on your gown before entering the Auditorium.

### 🚪 Doors Opening & Seating Times

•**Morning Session:** Doors open at 9.30am | Ceremony starts at 10.00am

•**Afternoon Session:** Doors open at 2.30pm | Ceremony starts at 3.00pm

•🪑 To ensure the ceremony begins on time, all graduands and guests must be seated in the Auditorium by:

•**9.50am (Morning Session)**

•**2.50pm (Afternoon Session)**

### ⚠️ Important:

•Once the ceremony has officially started, the **Auditorium doors will be closed**.

•**Latecomers will not be allowed** to enter the Auditorium.

✨ Dress smart, arrive early, and be ready for your special moment on stage!

# Useful Information

Additional Information:

Last updated 18 May 2026

## 👥 Guest Invitation

Each graduand may invite **up to 2 guests** to the ceremony. Please take note of the following:

🎟️ Admission into the Auditorium is **strictly by registration only**.

🪑 Seating is **limited** and available on a **first-come, first-served basis**.

If all Auditorium seats are filled, guests will be ushered to the **Function Hall (opposite the Auditorium)** to watch the live-stream of the ceremony.

⏰ Entry to the Auditorium begins at **9.30am (Morning Session)** and **2.30pm (Afternoon Session)**.

Guests should be seated by **9.50am (Morning Session)** and **2.50pm (Afternoon Session)**.

📵 Out of courtesy, guests are reminded to switch their mobile phones to **silent mode** inside the Auditorium.

🚫 Children **below 7 years old** will not be admitted into the Auditorium.

🙏 Guests are kindly requested to remain seated until the **entire ceremony concludes**.

Walk-ins or unregistered guests **cannot be accommodated**.

## 🚗 Carpark Information

Parking at **ITE Headquarters & ITE College Central** is **very limited**.

Guests who are driving are advised to park at the **nearby HDB carparks**.

✨ We look forward to welcoming your family and friends as they celebrate this proud milestone with you!

## 📸 Photo Taking

•Professional photographers will be present to take your photos on stage.

•Please advise your guests to refrain from taking photos during the Graduation Ceremony.

•Photographs will be available for download and details will be emailed to you after the event.

•We will be taking photos and videos at this event, which may be used in various communications platforms, including but not limited to publications, ITE website and social media platforms.

✨ Enjoy the moment—we’ll make sure your special day is beautifully captured!

## 🎖️ Guidelines for Receiving Your Certificate / Medal on Stage

To ensure a smooth and dignified ceremony, please follow these steps when it is your turn to go on stage:

### Queue Up

•The duty officer will usher you to the queue when it is time for you to receive your award.

•You will receive a **red certificate folder** before going on stage.

### Verification

•Have your **QR code ready** for scanning.

•This ensures your name is announced correctly by the Emcees.

### On Stage

•When your name is called, **walk smartly across the stage** and shake hands with the presenter.

•Follow the officer’s guidance to move to your **designated position** on stage.

### Group Photography (For All Graduands)

•Hold your certificate folder in your **right hand**, in front of you.

•Face the audience, relax, and **smile confidently**.

⚠️ Do not open the certificate folder on stage.

### For Course Medal Recipients

•Receive your medal with **both hands**.

•Follow the officer’s guidance to your designated position on stage.

•Hold your medal with **both hands, in front of you** while waiting for the group photo.

•Face the audience, relax, and smile.

✨ Remember: This is your moment—stand tall, smile, and enjoy the celebration of your achievement

### 📸 Group Photography & Exit from Stage

•When signalled by the officer and photographer, face the audience and photographer, and **smile confidently** for the group photo.

•After the photo is taken, move smartly to the other side of the stage and walk down in an orderly manner.

•Please observe **appropriate behaviour on stage** at all times.

•Your photo will be taken by the **official ITE photographer**.

⚠️ **Selfies or wefies on stage are not allowed**, as this is a formal ceremony to be respected by all graduands and their families.

### 📂 Certificate Folder (For All Graduands)

•The red certificate folder you receive on stage will **not contain any document**.

•Please **retain the folder** and collect your actual certificate after the ceremony:

•**Morning Session:** From 12.00pm onwards

•**Afternoon Session:** From 5.00pm onwards

•Collection Counter: **Classroom K424**

### 🏅 Course Medal Recipients

•The medal presented on stage will **not have your name engraved**.

•After leaving the stage, please **return the unengraved medal** to the duty officer.

•You may collect your actual engraved Course Medal after the ceremony at the same location:

•**Morning Session:** From 12.00pm onwards

•**Afternoon Session:** From 5.00pm onwards

•Collection Counter: **Classroom K424**

✨ Remember: Your stage moment will be captured professionally, so stand tall, smile, and make it a moment to cherish!

## ℹ️ Other Information

•There will be **no early collection** of certificates or medals.

•After receiving your certificate/medal on stage, you will be ushered back to your seat.

•Graduands must **remain in the Auditorium until the entire ceremony concludes**.

•To help make this celebration seamless and memorable for all participants, please observe **appropriate ceremony etiquette**.

### 📧 Contact Information

If you require further clarification on the **Work-Study Diploma Graduation Ceremony 2025**, please contact:✉️  [**rsvp@theevents.tech**](mailto:rsvp@theevents.tech)

The official **Graduation Ceremony website** will be **progressively updated** with the latest information.

✅ Do check back regularly for updates.

Thank you, and we look forward to celebrating this milestone with you!

# Information on Dress Code

Attire guidelines for attending graduands:

Last updated 18 May 2026

## WSDip Graduation Attire Information

All graduands attending the **WSDip Graduation Ceremony** will be required to wear the official **WSDip Graduation Attire**.

### Attire Requirements

Please note the following important points:

Graduands who are **not properly attired** or have **hair colour that is not of a natural tone** will **not** be registered and will **not** be permitted to go on stage to receive their certificate/medal.

### Rental and Purchase

The **WSDip** has appointed **My Uniform Shop** to manage the rental and sale of the WSDip Graduation Attire to graduands.

**[Please click** [here](https://www.myuniformshop.com.sg/ite-graduation) **for more details on renting / purchasing the graduation attire.]**

### The WSDip Graduation Attire

The official WSDip Graduation Attire consists of a **one-piece robe and detachable collar flap**. A common design is adopted for all graduands.

Male Graduand

Female Graduand

## Collar Flap Colour Chart

Please ensure that the **collar flap colour** is **correct** for your Graduation Ceremony.

The colour of the **detachable collar flap**, based on the graduand's qualification level, is shown below:

**Collar Flap Colour:**Red-Purple

**Level:**

- Technical Diploma
- Work-Study Diploma

## Recommended Dress Code

Graduands are advised to dress neatly and appropriately for this formal academic occasion. The WSDip graduation robe looks best with the following attire worn underneath:

Male Graduand

- White/light-coloured long-sleeved business shirt **with tie**
- Dark-coloured business pants*Note: National Servicemen (NSF) are expected to change into the recommended outfit*
- Dark-coloured office shoes with socks
- Short and neat hairdo (Coloured hair must be of a natural tone)

Female Graduand

- Blouse or dress with collar, preferably long or ¾ sleeved
- Skirt or dark-coloured dress pants*Note: The skirt length should be shorter than the graduation attire so the skirt does not hang below the graduation attire*
- Court shoes
- Neat hairdo (Coloured hair must be of a natural tone)

### Important Notes:

•Full-Time National Servicemen (NSF) are expected to change into the recommended outfit.

•Skirt length should be shorter than the graduation robe so the hem does not hang below the attire.

### Unacceptable Attire and Grooming

Graduands who are **not properly attired** or have hair colour that is not of a natural tone will **not** be registered and will **not** be permitted to go on stage to receive their certificate/medal.

**The following examples of dress and hair are strictly unacceptable:**

### Unacceptable Clothing & Footwear:

•Casual pants/jeans

•T-shirts, polo shirts, shorts, culottes, bermudas, and mini-skirts (females)

•Slippers, sneakers, sports shoes, **open-toe sandals, and open-toe shoes**

### Unacceptable Accessories & Grooming:

•Ear studs (for male graduands)

•Long fringe/long hair (for male graduands)

•**Coloured hair** that is not of a natural tone (e.g., grey, yellow, gold, blue, green, pink, purple, etc.)

# Course Fees and Financial Schemes for Full-time Technical Diploma

Find out more about the Course Fees and Financial Schemes for full-time Technical Diploma courses.

Last updated 25 June 2026

## Fee Structure for Full-time Technical Diploma Courses

ITE follows a cohort-based fee structure for full-time *Higher Nitec* and Technical Diploma courses. Under this structure, tuition fees remain unchanged throughout the course duration, providing students with greater certainty and helping them better plan their finances.

## Fees for Full-time Technical Diploma Students

AY2026 Course Fees (with MOE Tuition Grant)

| Course Fees | Singapore Citizen (SC) | Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Below 40 years old | 40 years old and above1 |  |
| Tuition Fee | S$3,100.00 / S$3,410.002 | S$2,100.00 / S$2,300.002 |
| Supplementary Fee | S$36.00 | S$36.00 |
| Examination Fee | - | - |
| Total Per Academic Year | S$3,136.00 / S$3,446.002 | S$2,136.00 / S$2,336.002 |

*1**With Skills Future Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidy.*

*2**Fees for Technical Diploma in Culinary Arts with Restaurant Management and Technical Diploma in Beauty and Wellness Management.*

- Fees shown are inclusive of GST or after GST subsidy.
- For details on fees for full-time Technical Diploma students admitted in each academic year, please  [read this document [PDF, 171 KB]](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/94d5ecd2-1019-4856-ab03-1382b620816f/AY2026_AY2025_Fees_TD_updated_13 Feb 2026.pdf) .
- For details on fees for full-time Technical Diploma students (Singapore Citizens aged 40 and above) admitted in each academic year, please  [read this document [PDF, 176 KB]](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/943a7ad2-6a33-4f23-8e0a-6d406278b799/AY2026_AY2025_MCES_Fees_TD_updated_12%20Dec%202025.pdf) .
- All fees are subject to changes as determined by MOE.

## MOE Tuition Grant Scheme

The Tuition Grant Scheme was introduced by the Government to help students with the costs of tertiary education in Singapore. The Tuition Grant Scheme is currently open to full-time Technical Diploma course students who have been admitted to ITE (subject to guidelines under existing policy).

MOE Tuition Grant Scheme

| Singapore Citizen (SC) | Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) |
| --- | --- |
| To be eligible, you must not have received tuition grant, subsidy, sponsorship, scholarship from the Singapore Government to obtain qualification levels that are same or higher than your course.#SC students will need to complete the MOE Tuition Grant Eligibility Declaration and submit it to your College during registration.If you are not eligible for the MOE Tuition Grant, you will have to pay the non-subsidised* tuition fee. | To be eligible, you must not have received tuition grant, subsidy, sponsorship, scholarship from the Singapore Government to obtain qualification levels that are same or higher than your course.To be considered and awarded with the Tuition Grant, SPR students are required to complete the Tuition Grant Eligibility Option and sign the Tuition Grant Agreement.SPR Tuition Grant recipients must serve a 3-year bond obligation upon graduation.If you do not apply or are not eligible for the MOE Tuition Grant, you will have to pay the non-subsidised* tuition fee. |

*# From Academic Year 2025, all Singapore Citizens aged 40 and above will qualify for Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidy for another full-time diploma programme offered at MOE-funded institutions, even if they had previously received government subsidies or sponsorship for a diploma or higher-level qualification.*

** Students who do not apply and / or sign the agreement with MOE within the stipulated application period will pay annual non-subsidised fees of about $22,900 to $23,210. Students who do not apply for MOE Tuition Grant will not be eligible for any financial assistance.*

Find out more about the  [Tuition Grant Scheme](https://go.gov.sg/tgwebsite) . If you have any enquiries on Tuition Grant matters, please contact the Ministry of Education at  [moe_tgonline@moe.gov.sg](mailto:moe_tgonline@moe.gov.sg) .

## SkillsFuture Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidy

You may use the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidy if you are a mid-career individual looking to upskill or reskill to remain competitive and resilient in the job market. You can apply for this subsidy if you meet all of the following criteria:

- A Singapore Citizen aged 40 and above in year of study.
- Qualify for the MOE/SSG base course fee subsidy. Those who are eligible will be charged the nett course fee.

For more information about SkillsFuture programmes and initiatives, please  [visit SkillsFuture](https://www.skillsfuture.gov.sg/enhancedsubsidy) .

## Financial Schemes for Fee Payment

Upon acceptance of the course, you may pay your first term fees through one of the following financial schemes:

Post-Secondary Education Scheme
Singapore Citizens may use their Post‑Secondary Education Account (PSEA) to pay the course fees for ITE Full‑time Technical Diploma. Please refer to the  [Fees](https://www.ite.edu.sg/current-full-time-students/admissions/fees/#dd498973198111da839058779a019ac1)  page for details on payment using PSEA.

For more information on PSEA, you may  [visit the MOE website](https://www.moe.gov.sg/financial-matters/psea) .CPF Education Loan Scheme
The CPF Education Loan Scheme is a loan scheme which allows you to use your own/your parent’s Ordinary Account (OA) savings to pay for your subsidised tuition fees. The total amount withdrawn for tuition fees plus accrued interest has to be repaid in full with cash. Repayment will start one year after date of graduation or date of leaving the institution, whichever is earlier. Interest starts accruing from the day of withdrawal, and is pegged to the prevailing CPF Ordinary Account interest rate which is currently 2.5% per annum.

- As students taking full-time government subsidised courses leading to a diploma at an approved local tertiary institution, you may apply for a loan from your own or your parents’ CPF savings to pay your tuition fees.
- New students who wish to apply for this scheme must submit the  [CPF Electronic Application](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/forms-e-applications/apply-for-cpf-education-loan)  during the CPF application period after your successful enrolment. Only online applications will be accepted.
- Students and the CPF members must each have a SingPass account in order to apply. If you or the CPF members do not have SingPass accounts, please apply with  [SingPass](https://www.singpass.gov.sg/main/) . CPF Board requires students to have email accounts.
- CPF Board also requires the CPF members to have email accounts as an email will be sent to members to login with their SingPass to give consent to the use of CPF savings for the students’ applications. CPF members must login using their own SingPass within 14 days from the date of the application, to agree to the use of their CPF savings. Otherwise, applications will be rejected.
- Students are required to print a copy of the successful e-application from CPF Board and submit it when you report to your posted campus for registration. Students can login to ‘ [My CPF Online Service](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/) ’ and check under ‘My Activities’ for the status of your application.

**Check** [**CPF's application schedule**](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/forms-e-applications/apply-for-cpf-education-loan/application-schedule) **for the application period and apply** [**here**](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/forms-e-applications/apply-for-cpf-education-loan) **.**

Application Dates

| Open date for CPF online application | Fri 6 Mar 2026 |
| --- | --- |
| Closing date for CPF application for both online and hardcopy application | Thu 19 Mar 2026 |

You can refer to  [CPF Board’s website](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/sub-categories?category=P_M_OS)  for more information on CPF Education Loan Scheme. For further queries, please contact CPF Board on Tel: 1800-227-1188.Mendaki Tertiary Tuition Fee Subsidy
The Tertiary Tuition Fee Subsidy (TTFS) scheme, introduced in 1991, is an education subsidy for Malay students which covers their tuition fees at tertiary institutions.

You are eligible for the Tertiary Tuition Fee Subsidy (TTFS) only if you satisfy all the conditions below:

1. You are a Singapore Citizen or a Permanent Resident of Singapore with one of your parents (natural, adoptive or step parent), living or deceased, a Singapore Citizen.
2. Your race or the first component of the double-barrelled race is Malay (which includes Boyanese, Javanese, Banjarese Bugis and Indo extract) e.g. for double-race Malay-Indian.
3. You are eligible for MOE Tuition Grant.
4. You are pursuing a diploma or degree on full-time basis at a local government tertiary institution
5. Your monthly household per capita income (PCI) does not exceed $2,400.

PCI = Total gross monthly income of all working family members / Number of family members in the same household

| Per Capita Income (PCI) | Eligible Subsidy |
| --- | --- |
| S$1,700 and belowS$1,701 - S$2,000S$2,001 – S$2,200S$2,201 – S$2,400 | 100%75%50%25% |

Note: TTFS covers only tuition fees (other fees such as supplementary fees, examination fees, study tour or overseas exchange programme are not covered).

Application Period

| How to Apply | Log on toMendaki Tertiary Tuition Fee Subsidy. Only online applications will be accepted. |
| --- | --- |
| 1st Application Period | 25 Feb 2026 – 30 Apr 2026 |
| 2nd Application Period | 16 Sep 2026 - 31 Oct 2026 |

For more information, you may refer to  [MENDAKI](https://www.mendaki.org.sg/) ’s website. You may also contact MENDAKI at  [https://www.mendaki.org.sg/contact-us](https://www.mendaki.org.sg/contact-us) .

**Additional Loan Scheme: Study Loan (Full-Time Local National)**

MENDAKI also offers study loan scheme for eligible full-time local students. The scheme is open to Malay / Muslim Singaporeans pursuing a full-time Diploma at local government institutions, including Polytechnics and ITE.

**Application Period:**25 Feb 2026 - 18 Nov 2026

For more information, you may refer to  [Mendaki Study Loan Schemes](https://www.mendaki.org.sg/scheme-listing) .Higher Education Student Loan Scheme
From 29 July 2026, the new Higher Education Student Loan (HESL) scheme will be implemented to provide loans to students who need help to finance their tertiary studies when they pursue approved MOE-subsidised diploma at the publicly-funded post-secondary education institutions (PSEIs).

The HESL will provide loans to cover the tuition fees payable and an annual living allowance. The scheme is interest-free during the course of study, with interest commencing only upon a student’s graduation or leaving their institution. The maximum loan repayment period for the HESL scheme is 10 years.

Before taking up HESL, students should first consider other financing options, such as government bursaries, Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA) fund and institution-based financial aid schemes.

HESL Scheme Details

| HESL Component | Who are Eligible | Loan Provision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Base Provision | Full-time diploma students [Singapore Citizens (SC) and Singapore Permanent Residents (SPR)] |
| 2 | Means-tested Provision |  |
| a | Balance Fee Coverage | Full-time diploma students (SC) |
| b | Living Allowance Loan | Full-time diploma students (SC and SPR) |

Application Details

| How to Apply | Students who wish to apply for the HESL can do so via the new StudentLoanSG (SLSG) portal (https://go.gov.sg/slsg). |
| --- | --- |
| Who can Apply | The portal will accept HESL applications from the following students, who may apply using their Singpass accounts:(a) Newly matriculated students in Academic Year (AY) 2026 intake; and(b) Existing students (prior to AY2026 intake).The HESL is made up of 2 components:Non-means tested base provision for all students (SC and SPR) that can cover up to 90% of the subsidised fees payable, depending on the citizenship of the student.Means-tested provision*:(i) For eligible SC students – covers the balance of their tuition fees not covered by the base provision and loan for living allowance.(ii) For eligible SPR – covers loan for living allowance only.*SC and SPR with gross monthly household per capita income (PCI) of $3,500 or less. |
| Commencement Date | 29 Jul 2026, 10am |

For more information on HESL Scheme, you may visit  [https://www.moe.gov.sg/financial-matters/government-loan-scheme/higher-education-student-loan](https://www.moe.gov.sg/financial-matters/government-loan-scheme/higher-education-student-loan) .SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career)
This credit supports Singapore Citizens aged 40 and above. It can be used to offset out-of-pocket course fees for selected course that have better employability outcomes, and it does not expire.

For more information about SkillsFuture Credits, visit  [https://www.myskillsfuture.gov.sg/content/portal/en/career-resources/career-resources/education-career-personal-development/SkillsFuture_Credit.html.](https://www.myskillsfuture.gov.sg/content/portal/en/career-resources/career-resources/education-career-personal-development/SkillsFuture_Credit.html)

Learn more about the various  [Bursaries](https://www.ite.edu.sg/current-full-time-students/scholarships--awards---bursaries/bursaries/)  and  [Financial Assistance Schemes](https://www.ite.edu.sg/current-full-time-students/admissions/student-services/financial-assistance/)  available.

Find out more on the  [SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme](https://www.myskillsfuture.gov.sg/content/portal/en/career-resources/career-resources/education-career-personal-development/SkillsFuture_Level-Up_Programme.html)  for Singapore Citizens aged 40 and above.

Find out more on the  [Workfare Skills Support (WSS) (Level-Up)](https://www.wsg.gov.sg/home/individuals/attachment-placement-programmes/workfare-skills-support-levelup)  for Singapore Citizens aged 30 and above with an average gross monthly income of not more than $3,000 for the past 12 months.

4. Early Admissions Exercise (EAE)

# Early Admissions Exercise (EAE)

More information about EAE for Higher Nitec courses.

Last updated 5 May 2026

## What is ITE EAE?

The ITE Early Admissions Exercise (ITE EAE) is an aptitude-based admissions exercise. If you have strong aptitude and passion in a field related to a *Higher Nitec* course, the ITE EAE is for you. We will also consider your relevant work experience and your achievements in sports, arts, leadership, entrepreneurship and community service.

If you are a student from a Specialised School for Normal Technical (SSNT), you will have an added advantage if you apply to a course that is related to your ITE Skills Subject Certificate (ISSC).

The application process involves an interview for each of your course choices (if shortlisted).

**If your application is successful, you will receive a conditional offer for admission to one of your course of choices for the next intake.**

Your place in the course will be confirmed if you accept the conditional offer **and** your GCE N/O-Level or final *Nitec* examination results meet the Minimum Entry Requirements of the course.

- [Factsheet on ITE EAE (for GCE N/O-Level students)](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/e4006761-568f-4d1a-b13a-739673587765/ITE-EAE-2027-Intake-Factsheet.pdf)
- [Factsheet on ITE EAE (for *Nitec* students)](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/e635b70a-8d35-46c1-9036-d8dcf4da67b7/ITE-EAEP-2027-Intake-Factsheet.pdf)

## Who can apply

### For GCE N/O-Level students:

- Singapore Citizens (SC) and Singapore Permanent Residents (SPR) who have registered to sit for the GCE N/O-Level examinations in the year of the ITE EAE application;
- International Students (IS) enrolled in Government, Government-aided and Independent Schools during the year of the ITE EAE application, and who have registered to sit for the GCE N/O-Level examinations in the year of the ITE EAE application;
- SC and SPR who have sat for the GCE N/O-Level examinations previously; and
- SC and SPR working adults with at least 2 years of relevant work experience may also apply.

### For Nitec-progression students:

- SC, SPR and IS full-time *Nitec* or Traineeship students who will graduate in the same ITE academic year as the ITE EAEP;
- SC and SPR who have graduated from ITE full-time *Nitec* or Traineeship courses; and
- SC and SPR working adults with *Nitec* qualification and at least 2 years of relevant work experience may also apply.

### Direct entry to the 2nd year of Higher Nitec courses

*Nitec* students who wish to apply for direct entry to 2nd year of *Higher Nitec* courses should apply to *Higher Nitec* courses that are mapped to their *Nitec* course. Successful ITE EAEP applicants will be given a conditional offer for admission to the 1st year of the *Higher Nitec* course. Subsequently, students who meet the GPA requirement for direct entry to 2nd year of mapped *Higher Nitec* courses will be considered for direct entry to 2nd year (subject to merit and vacancies) alongside other *Nitec* students who applied through the *Nitec* Progression to *Higher Nitec* Intake Exercise (NCHN). *Nitec* students seeking direct entry to the 2nd year of a *Higher Nitec* course should note that the ITE EAEP conditional offer does not guarantee admission to the 2nd year of the *Higher Nitec* course, even if their final *Nitec* results meet the eligibility criteria as places are limited.

### Deferment of National Service (NS) for NS-liable males

NS-liable males will be granted NS deferment for the pursuit of full-time studies at pre-university government-funded institutions including ITE if they attain a place and are pursuing a course for higher academic qualifications from what they have previously attained (e.g. from N/O Levels to *Nitec/Higher Nitec*, from *Nitec* to *Higher Nitec* or from *Nitec/Higher Nitec* to ITE Work-Study Diploma/Technical Engineer Diploma/Technical Diploma courses) and NS deferment will no longer be subject to cut-off ages.

For latest updates on NS deferment eligibility and policy, please visit the  [NS Deferment page.](https://for.edu.sg/ns-deferment)  Students who are not eligible for NS deferment will need to withdraw from the course that they are enrolled in.

NS-enlisted males who plan to disrupt their NS for the pursuit of full-time studies at pre-university government-funded institutions including ITE can visit  [NS Disruption](https://www.ns.gov.sg/web/profiles/nsf/impt-full-time-ns-info#disruption-of-ftns)  page for more information.

## Application process

### Application

**Wed 20 May - Tue 26 May 2026**

You can apply for up to 3 course choices. Courses with the same title at different ITE Colleges are counted as separate choices. You are not allowed to change your course choices after the close of application.

In your application, tell us why you should be shortlisted for an interview through a write-up (up to around 100 words) for each course choice. List down your talents, aptitude, achievements, passion and interests relevant to the course, including:

- Portfolio of related projects
- Participation in MOE Elective Modules, Applied Learning Modules (ApLM), Applied Subjects, ITE Skills Subjects, and/or ITE Elective Modules
- Participation in work attachments, community/volunteer work, school/personal activities/projects, CCAs and competitions e.g. ignITE Skills Challenge, etc. that are related to the applied ITE course(s)
- Relevant work experience

#### Tips

- Prepare your write-up in advance using  [this template](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/07aa0275-7384-44b8-b776-198288e32128/ite-eae-writeup-preparation-template 2027.pdf)
- **[New] Upload documents to cloud storage and create a shareable download link**: Prepare soft copies of relevant supporting documents, such as certificates of achievement, work testimonials, and portfolios (if applicable), as evidence for information in your write-ups and official GCE N- or O-Level examination results (only for applicants who have sat for the GCE examinations previously). Upload these documents to online cloud storage and create a shareable download link for submission with your online application. Ensure that the download link is set to 'public'.
- Save/print your write-up to help you recall the details when preparing for your interview
- Retain your login ID and password provided in the verification slip after submitting your application. You will need them later when checking your application result and accepting your offer.

To submit your application, proceed to the intake webpage for:

- [GCE N/O Level students](/intake-exercises/for-secondary-school-students-and-gce-holders/)
- [Nitec students progressing to Higher Nitec courses](/intake-exercises/for-nitec-progression-to-higher-nitec/)

To submit an application, you will need to login with your personal Singpass. You cannot use your parent’s Singpass.

If you encounter Singpass issues, please visit the  [Singpass website](https://portal.singpass.gov.sg/home/ui/login)  for information on Singpass application and password reset. For further assistance, please refer to the  [Singpass FAQ page](https://ask.gov.sg/singpass) , call the Singpass helpdesk at +65 6335 3533 or email  [support@singpass.gov.sg](mailto:support@singpass.gov.sg)

### Interview

**Mon 15 Jun - Wed 22 Jul 2026**

Interviews will be conducted either online or on-campus. If you are shortlisted, the respective ITE College will notify you of the interview details via email, phone call or SMS.

Bring along to the interview your portfolio of relevant works/projects and supporting documents, such as certificates, awards and testimonials, for us to assess your aptitude and interest for the course. You may also have to take an aptitude test when attending the interview, depending on the course.

You will be notified to attend up to one interview for your choices with the same course title at two or more ITE Colleges.

### Offer and acceptance phase

**Mon 17 Aug - Fri 21 Aug 2026**

Log in to  [https://student.ite.edu.sg](https://student.ite.edu.sg)  to check your application result.

If your application is successful, you must accept the offer online by **end of acceptance deadline**. Otherwise your offer will be withdrawn.

You will be guaranteed a place in the course if you accept the offer, as long as your GCE N/O-Level / Nitec final examination results meet the Minimum Entry Requirements of the course.

### Withdrawal phase

**Mon 24 Aug - Fri 28 Aug 2026**

If you decide to withdraw from the offer after having accepted it earlier, you must submit your withdrawal request to  [training@ite.edu.sg](mailto:training@ite.edu.sg)  by **end of withdrawal deadline.**

If you do not withdraw by **end of withdrawal deadline** and your GCE N/O-Level / Nitec final examination results meet the Minimum Entry Requirements, your place in the course will be confirmed.

### Confirmation of Conditional Offer

**After release of GCE N/O-Level / Nitec final examination results**

If you have accepted a conditional offer, your GCE N/O-Level / Nitec final examination results must also meet the Minimum Entry Requirements for your place to be confirmed.

ITE will inform you of your offer confirmation status shortly after the official release of GCE N/O-Level / Nitec final examination results.

# Entry qualifications

More information about admissions based on your relevant qualifications.

Last updated 19 June 2026

**Congratulations to all GCE 'N' and 'O' Level holders for completing your secondary school education!**

Now you can begin your journey to a successful career by enrolling in ITE's post-secondary ITE courses. With a wide range of courses to choose from in Business & Services, Design & Media, Electronics & Info-Comm Technology, Engineering, Health Sciences and Hospitality, you can be certain of finding one that is right for you.

## Intakes by entry qualifications

### [Application for GCE 'O' Level students](/secondary-school-students/admissions/entry-qualifications/gce-o-level/)

### [Application for GCE 'N' Level students](/secondary-school-students/admissions/entry-qualifications/gce-n-level/)

### [Applicants combining GCE 'N' or GCE 'O' results of 2 sittings](/secondary-school-students/admissions/entry-qualifications/applicants-combining-gce-results/)

### [Application for ITE Skills Certificate ISC graduates](/secondary-school-students/admissions/entry-qualifications/ite-skills-certificate/)

### [Applications for students with other qualifications (for 2026 intake)](/secondary-school-students/admissions/entry-qualifications/other-qualifications/)

## List of ITE courses

- [3-year/ 4-year Higher Nitec (for GCE N & O students)](/secondary-school-students/ite-full-time-courses/3-year-4-year-higher-nitec/)
- [2-year Higher Nitec (for GCE O students & Nitec graduates)](/current-full-time-students/progression/higher-nitec/)
- [2-year Higher Nitec (for DPP GCE N(A) students)](/secondary-school-students/ite-full-time-courses/higher-nitec-for-dpp/)

## Course advising

For general course advising, applicants may  [make an appointment online](/current-full-time-students/admissions/student-services/education---career-guidance--ecg-/)  with one of our Education & Career Guidance (ECG) Counsellors.

The offer of an ITE course to applicants is subject to them being physically, medically and mentally fit to pursue the course. This is to ensure that all students can benefit from ITE training in a safe and conducive environment.

Applicants or students assessed by ITE as being unfit can be withdrawn from the course. Where appropriate, they may be considered for other courses if there are suitable ones. The Learning Accessibility Office (LAO) at each ITE College will provide support to students with special educational needs in their learning process at ITE.

Applicants with special educational needs are strongly encouraged to  [seek prior academic course advising from the respective College(s)](/current-full-time-students/admissions/student-services/learning-accessibility/)  before selecting their choice of application.

## Deferment of National Service (NS) for NS-liable males/ Disruption of NS for NS-enlisted males

NS-liable males will be granted NS deferment for the pursuit of full-time studies at pre-university government-funded institutions including ITE if they attain a place and are pursuing a course for higher academic qualifications from what they have previously attained (e.g. from N/O Levels to Higher Nitec, from Nitec to Higher Nitec or from Nitec/Higher Nitec to ITE Work-Study Diploma/Technical Engineer Diploma/Technical Diploma courses) and NS deferment will no longer be subject to cut-off ages.

For latest updates on NS deferment eligibility and policy, please visit the  [NS Deferment page](https://for.edu.sg/ns-deferment) . Students who are not eligible for NS deferment will need to withdraw from the course that they are enrolled in.

NS-enlisted males who plan to disrupt their NS for the pursuit of full-time studies at pre-university government-funded institutions including ITE can visit  [NS Disruption](https://www.ns.gov.sg/web/profiles/nsf/impt-full-time-ns-info#disruption-of-ftns)  page for more information.

# Joint Admissions Exercise (JAE)

Find out more about the application for full-time 2-year Higher Nitec courses (Apr 2026 intake).

Last updated 30 April 2026

The Joint Admissions Exercise (JAE) caters to the intake of GCE ‘O’ Level holders into full-time 2-year Higher Nitec courses. JAE is held in January each year, after the release of the GCE ‘O’ Level results. Successful applicants will commence their training in April.

Admission to the courses is based on merit and choice.

You may also refer to the Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) for information on admissions under JAE. If you need help with your application, please call or email to any of the  [Customer & Visitor Centres at ITE Colleges](/about-ite/contact-us/)  during office hours.

## Before applying

- [Application schedule [PDF, 140 KB]](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/877b55bb-90be-4df0-b010-81beea0fb186/JAE-2026-Intake-Application-Schedule (tentative for MOE JAE result release).pdf)
- [ITE courses offered, minimum entry requirements, previous year net aggregate range and compute your JAE aggregate [PDF, 333 KB]](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/b18b2ccb-7d0b-4e89-ba0a-fd0731ddba83/JAE-2026-Entry-Requirements.pdf)

## Submit your application

Refer to step-by-step  [Application / Appeal guide](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/4885e75e-5056-4b0a-866b-0233d7c17c8a/JAE-2026-Application-Appeal-Guide.pdf)  for details on application process and appeal for admission or transfer.

**A. MOE JAE (Main Phase)**

Application under MOE JAE (main phase) is now closed.

**B. Combined Polytechnic-ITE JAE Appeal**

Submission of appeal under Combined Polytechnic-ITE JAE Appeal phase is now closed.

**C. Final JAE ITE Appeal**

Submission of appeal under Final JAE ITE Appeal phase is now closed.

**Pre-course evaluation for 2-year*****Higher Nitec*****in Nursing course**

Applicants posted to the 2-year *Higher Nitec* in Nursing course must attend a pre-course evaluation at ITE College East scheduled on the following dates, before they can accept their course offer:

- On **Wed 4 Feb 2026**for those posted under MOE JAE (Main Phase)

- On **Tue 24 Feb 2026** for those posted under Combined Polytechnic-ITE JAE Appeal

## Course acceptance

- Refer to step-by-step  [Acceptance guide](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/04ce779a-9152-4efb-8258-fd8a599e5ad3/Apr-2026-HNitec-Acceptance-Guide.pdf)  for details on how to complete the course acceptance process
- Applicants may login to  [https://student.ite.edu.sg](https://student.ite.edu.sg)  to check your application result via 'Student Admission' > 'View Application Results’

### Final JAE ITE Appeal - Appeal Result & Acceptance of Offer

Applicants can check appeal result **between Thu 12 Mar 2026 and Mon 13 Apr 2026 (for appeals submitted under 1****st****sub-phase)**, and **between Mon 13 Apr 2026 and Thu 30 Apr 2026 (for appeals submitted under 2****nd****sub-phase)**.

## Reporting to college

- Successful applicants who have accepted their course offer have to report to their posted ITE College by the stipulated date to register for their course
- If you are an International Applicant (i.e. not Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident) and had sat for the Singapore-Cambridge GCE 'O' Level examination as candidate of a Government, Government-Aided or Independent school in Singapore) who has accepted the course offer, you should report to College only after receiving your Student's Pass from the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA) to study in ITE, or if you have a valid Immigration Pass (e.g. Dependant's Pass / Long-Term Visit Pass). Instructions on applying for your Student's Pass are provided in your Enrolment Letter (emailed to you upon release of application outcome).
- Refer to  [Guide to complete your registration](https://for.edu.sg/college-reporting-apr-intake)  for details

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

Refer to the  [FAQs](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/02de4e60-d167-4e1a-aa44-50ceef017642/JAE-2026-WebFAQ.pdf)  for Joint Admissions Exercise (JAE).

# Joint Intake Exercise 'O' (JIE 'O')

Find out more about the application for full-time 3-year Higher Nitec courses (Jan 2026 intake).

Last updated 19 June 2026

The Joint Intake Exercise 'O' (JIE 'O') caters to the intake of GCE ‘O’ Level holders into full-time 3-year Higher Nitec courses. JIE 'O' is held in January each year, after the release of the GCE ‘O’ Level results. Successful applicants will commence their training in January.

Admission to the courses is based on merit and choice.

You may also refer to the Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) for information on admissions under JIEO. If you need help with your application, please call or email to any of the  [Customer & Visitor Centres at ITE Colleges](/about-ite/contact-us/)  during office hours.

## Before applying

- [Application schedule [PDF, 117 KB]](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/61f47348-cffe-45f2-80be-382579a84a1f/JIEO-2026-Intake-Application-Schedule.pdf)
- [Courses offered and minimum entry requirements [PDF, 271 KB]](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/4b548162-fe00-41bf-9630-01c292dbda43/JIEO-2026-Intake-Entry-Requirements .pdf)

## Submit your application

- Refer to step-by-step  [Application guide](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/a438479b-836a-4d22-a457-e979f2cbd300/JIEO-2026-Intake-How-to-Apply.pdf)  for details on application process
- Refer to step-by-step  [Appeal guide](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/110661a5-c527-44cd-8712-ec5bc9799fd1/JIEO-2026-Intake-How-to-Appeal.pdf)  for details for instructions on appeal for admission or transfer

### Main application phase

Application opens from **Wed 14 Jan 2026 (4pm)** to**Mon 19 Jan 2026 (4.30pm)**.[Application has closed]

### Appeal Application Phase

**Appeal for Admission / Transfer (under Appeal Phase)**

Unsuccessful applicants appealing for admission, and students appealing for transfer, may submit their appeal online (under JIE ‘N’) between **Thu 22 Jan 2026 and Fri 6 Feb 2026** (2nd sub-phase).

**Pre-course evaluation for 3-year Higher Nitec in Nursing course**

• Pre-course evaluation for 3-year Higher Nitec in Nursing will be conducted on **Fri 23 Jan 2026.**

## Course acceptance

- Refer to step-by-step  [Acceptance guide](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/b5bdcb3d-acbb-449f-9774-5a696f89ddda/JIEO-2026-Intake-How-to-Do-Course-Acceptance.pdf)  for details on how to complete the course acceptance process
- Applicants may login to  [https://student.ite.edu.sg](https://student.ite.edu.sg)  to check your application result via 'Student Admission'>'View Application Results'

### Main Application Phase

**Application Result & Acceptance of Offer**

Application result will be released on **Thu 22 Jan 2026 (9am)**.

Successful applicants are required to login and accept the course offer online between **Thu 22 Jan 2026 (9am) and Mon 26 Jan 2026.**

## Reporting to college

- Successful applicants who have accepted their course offer have to report to their posted ITE College by the stipulated dates to register for their course
- If you are an International Applicant (i.e. not SC or SPR) and had sat for the Singapore-Cambridge GCE 'O' level examination as candidate of a Government, Government-Aided or Independent school in Singapore) who has accepted the course offer, you should report to College only after receiving your Student's Pass from the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA) to study in ITE, or if you have a valid Immigration Pass (e.g. Dependant’s Pass / Long-Term Visit Pass). Instructions on applying for your Student's Pass are provided in your Enrolment Letter (emailed to you upon release of application outcome).
- Refer to  [Guide to complete your registration](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/5b95e335-d948-4d70-bafb-01dfb516c7b8/Registration Guide (3-yr HN JIEO).pdf)  for details

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

View the related  [FAQs](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/fad1d80a-6933-4cff-a3f8-403fbe86d4f3/JIEO-2026-Intake-FAQs.pdf)  under **Full-Time Education > Joint Intake Exercise 'O' (JIE 'O')**

# Joint Intake Exercise 'N' (JIE 'N')|GCE 'O' Level Students

Find out more about the application for full-time 3-year Higher Nitec courses (Jan 2026 intake).

Last updated 19 June 2026

The Joint Intake Exercise 'N' (JIE 'N') caters to the intake of GCE ‘N’ Level holders into full-time 3-year Higher Nitec courses. GCE ‘O’ Level holders may also apply. JIE 'N' is held in December each year, after the release of the GCE ‘N’ Level results. Successful applicants will commence their training in January.

Admission to the courses is based on merit and choice.

You may also refer to the Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) for information on admissions under JIEN. If you need help with your application, please call or email to any of the  [Customer & Visitor Centres at ITE Colleges](/about-ite/contact-us/)  during office hours.

## 1. Before applying

- [Application schedule [PDF, 101 KB]](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/a856401b-633f-49b8-90e3-237957fddf47/JIEN_JIEE 2026 Intake Application Schedule.pdf)
- [Courses offered, minimum entry requirements, previous year ITE aggregate points and compute your ITE aggregate points [PDF, 388 KB]](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/7da0f46d-13f5-4a23-aa9f-5fda36e5ecd2/JIEN_JIEE 2026 Intake entry requirements.pdf)

- Refer to step-by-step  [Appeal guide](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/053e307e-29ac-4e7f-832b-65e2f142697e/JIEN_JIEE 2026 Intake Appeal Instructions.pdf)  for details on appeal for admission or transfer

### Final Appeal Application Phase

**Appeal for Admission / Transfer (under Final Appeal Phase)**

Unsuccessful applicants appealing for admission, and students appealing for transfer, may submit their appeal online under the final appeal phase.

Appeals can be submitted between **Fri 9 Jan 2026** and **Fri 16 Jan 2026** (1st sub-phase), and between **Thu 22 Jan 2026** and **Fri 6 Feb 2026** (2nd sub-phase).

### Pre-course evaluation for 3-year Higher Nitec in Nursing course

- Pre-course evaluation for 3-year Higher Nitec in Nursing will be conducted on **Mon 29 Dec 2025 to Tue 30 Dec 2025** under Main application phase and **Wed 7 Jan 2026** under Appeal phase.

## 3. Course acceptance

- Refer to step-by-step  [Acceptance guide](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/1b52f3aa-86fe-4238-9aef-e2ba457d7f7f/JIEN_JIEE 2026 Intake Acceptance Instructions.pdf)  for details on how to complete the course acceptance process
- Applicants may login to  [https://student.ite.edu.sg](https://student.ite.edu.sg/psp/CS92PRD/?cmd=login&languageCd=ENG&)  to check your application result via 'Self-Service'>'Student Admission'>'View Application Results'

**Final Appeal Phase**

**Application Result & Acceptance of Offer**

Applicants can log in to check the outcome of appeal between **Mon 12 Jan 2026** and **Thu 22 Jan 2026** (for appeals submitted under 1st sub-phase), and between **Thu 22 Jan 2026** and **Wed 11 Feb 2026** (for appeals submitted under 2nd sub-phase)

## 4. Reporting to college

- Successful applicants who have accepted their course offer have to report to their posted ITE College by the stipulated dates to register for their course
- If you are an International Applicant (i.e. not SC or SPR) and had sat for the Singapore-Cambridge GCE level examination as candidate of a Government, Government-Aided or Independent school in Singapore) who has accepted the course offer, you should report to College only after receiving your Student Pass from the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA) to study in ITE, or if you have a valid Immigration Pass (e.g. Dependant’s Pass / Long-Term Visit Pass). Instructions on applying for your Student Pass are provided in your Enrolment Letter (emailed to you upon release of application outcome).
- Refer to  [Guide to complete your registration](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/87d39595-5809-4e1e-9dd3-9e711b6bfbfb/Copy of Registration Guide (Nitec & 3-yr HN)_updated 11 Dec.pdf)  for details

Find out more about the application for full-time 3-year Higher Nitec courses (Jan 2026 intake).

Last updated 19 June 2026

The Joint Intake Exercise 'N' (JIE 'N') caters to the intake of GCE ‘N’ Level holders into full-time 3-year Higher Nitec courses. GCE ‘O’ Level holders may also apply. JIE 'N' is held in December each year, after the release of the GCE ‘N’ Level results. Successful applicants will commence their training in January.

Admission to the courses is based on merit and choice.

You may also refer to the Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) for information on admissions under JIEN. If you need help with your application, please call or email to any of the  [Customer & Visitor Centres at ITE Colleges](/about-ite/contact-us/)  during office hours.

## 1. Before applying

- [Application schedule [PDF, 101 KB]](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/8ab23589-8718-4fb3-9088-fd2312a4ecc3/JIEN_JIEE 2026 Intake Application Schedule.pdf)
- [Courses offered, minimum entry requirements, previous year ITE aggregate points and compute your ITE aggregate points [PDF, 388 KB]](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/097d74ce-8353-4a03-b0b1-f12b5822d473/JIEN_JIEE 2026 Intake entry requirements.pdf)

## 2. Submit your application

- Refer to step-by-step  [Application guide](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/becdea5e-8dc6-40a5-a832-db690e599dd9/JIEN_JIEE_2026 Intake Application Instructions.pdf)  for details on application process
- Refer to step-by-step  [Appeal guide](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/38bee992-dd6c-4944-b162-f58233aa2e19/JIEN_JIEE 2026 Intake Appeal Instructions.pdf) for details on appeal for admission or transfer

**Final Appeal Application Phase**

**Appeal for Admission / Transfer (under Final Appeal Phase)**

Unsuccessful applicants appealing for admission, and students appealing for transfer, may submit their appeal online under the final appeal phase.

Appeals can be submitted between **Fri 9 Jan 2026** and **Fri 16 Jan 2026** (1st sub-phase), and between **Thu 22 Jan 2026** and **Fri 6 Feb 2026** (2nd sub-phase).

### Pre-course evaluation for 3-year Higher Nitec in Nursing course

- Pre-course evaluation for 3-year Higher Nitec in Nursing will be conducted on **Mon 29 Dec 2025 to Tue 30 Dec 2025** under Main application phase and **Wed 7 Jan 2026** under Appeal phase

## 3. Course acceptance

- Refer to step-by-step  [Acceptance guide](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/f9816548-81bf-4f62-9562-22c1b1dabe98/JIEN_JIEE 2026 Intake Acceptance Instructions.pdf)  for details on how to complete the course acceptance process
- Applicants may login to  [https://student.ite.edu.sg](https://student.ite.edu.sg/psp/CS92PRD/?cmd=login&languageCd=ENG&)  to check your application result via 'Student Admission'>'View Application Results'

**Final Appeal Application Phase**

**Application Result & Acceptance of Offer**

Applicants can log in to check the outcome of appeal between **Mon 12 Jan 2026** and **Thu 22 Jan 2026** (for appeals submitted under 1st sub-phase), and between **Thu 22 Jan 2026** and **Wed 11 Feb 2026** (for appeals submitted under 2nd sub-phase)

## 4. Reporting to college

- Successful applicants who have accepted their course offer have to report to their posted ITE College by the stipulated dates to register for their course
- If you are an International Applicant (i.e. not SC or SPR) and had sat for the Singapore-Cambridge GCE level examination as candidate of a Government, Government-Aided or Independent school in Singapore) who has accepted the course offer, you should report to College only after receiving your Student Pass from the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA) to study in ITE, or if you have a valid Immigration Pass (e.g. Dependant’s Pass / Long-Term Visit Pass). Instructions on applying for your Student Pass are provided in your Enrolment Letter (emailed to you upon release of application outcome).
- Refer to  [Guide to complete your registration](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/7a252769-60c1-4d9f-beba-d6ecca0700b5/Copy of Registration Guide (Nitec & 3-yr HN)_updated 11 Dec.pdf)  for details

# Joint Intake Exercise 'H' (JIE 'H')

Find out more about the application for full-time 2-year Higher Nitec courses (Jan 2026 intake).

Last updated 10 February 2026

The Joint Intake Exercise 'H' (JIE 'H') caters to the direct entry of eligible GCE N(A) holders into full-time 2-year Higher Nitec courses, under the Direct Entry Scheme to Polytechnic Programme (DPP). JIE 'H' is held in December each year, after the release of the GCE 'N' Level results. Successful applicants will commence their training in January.

Only Sec 4N(A) students of the preceding cohort, i.e. only scores received by Sec 4N(A) students at the GCE 'N' Level examinations in 2025 will be considered for application to the DPP 2026 intake.

Admission to the courses is based on merit and choice.

Eligible GCE N(A) applicants can apply for both 2-year Higher Nitec courses under JIE 'H', and 3-year Higher Nitec courses under JIE 'N'. An applicant who is successful for a 2-year Higher Nitec course under JIE 'H' will not be offered a 3-year Higher Nitec course under JIE 'N'.

You may also refer to the Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) for information on admissions under JIEH. If you need help with your application, please call or email to any of the  [Customer & Visitor Centres at ITE Colleges](/about-ite/contact-us/)  during office hours.

- [Application schedule [PDF, 137 KB]](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/3eef14d2-967e-41fa-9770-78e6a025e224/DPP 2026 - Application Schedule - XG.pdf)

- Refer to step-by-step  [Appeal guide](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/caac324f-9543-4db6-9fde-aed90bbe0cdb/DPP 2026 - Appeal Instructions - XG.pdf)  for details on appeal process

### Final Appeal Phase

Unsuccessful applicants appealing for admission, and students appealing for transfer, may submit their appeal online between **Wed 21 Jan 2026** and **Mon 2 Feb 2026**. [Appeal application has closed]

## 3. Course acceptance

- Refer to step-by-step  [Acceptance guide](https://isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg/145/95c576a2-e8e3-45fa-a94f-4abf94dc7148/DPP 2026 - Acceptance Procedure - XG.pdf)  for details on how to complete the course acceptance process

- If you are an International Applicant (i.e. not SC or SPR) and had sat for the Singapore-Cambridge GCE level examination as candidate of a Government, Government-Aided or Independent school in Singapore) who has accepted the course offer, you should report to College only after receiving your Student Pass from the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA) to study in ITE, or if you have a valid Immigration Pass (e.g. Dependent’s Pass / Long-Term Visit Pass). JIE 'E' is held in December each year, after the release of the GCE ‘N’ Level results. Successful applicants will commence their training in January.

Admission to the courses is based on merit and choice. Eligible GCE N(T) applicants can apply for courses under both JIE 'N' and JIE 'E' concurrently. Please note that you will receive only 1 offer even if you are successful in both applications.

# Certification system

More information about the certification system for full-time / part-time education, traineeship programmes and Work-Study programmes.

Last updated 27 August 2025

The ITE Certification System comprises certification levels as follows:

## Full-time education

- **National ITE Certificate (*****Nitec*****)** for courses that require completion of GCE ‘N’ Level or GCE ‘O’ Level as an entry requirement, with pre-requisites for certain courses.
- **Higher National ITE Certificate (*****Higher Nitec*****)** for courses that require GCE ‘O’ Level or GCE 'N' (Academic) Level with pre-requisites as an entry requirement.
- **Technical Diploma** for courses that require relevant *Higher Nitec* / *Nitec* as an entry requirement.

## Traineeship programmes

- Some*Nitec* and *Higher Nitec* courses are offered in traineeship mode as well. Entry requirements are similar to related courses in full-time education.

## Work-Study programmes

- **Work-Study Diploma**for courses that are in partnership with employers targeted at ITE Graduates with relevant *Higher Nitec* / *Nitec* or relevant working experience as an entry requirement.

## Part-time Education

- **National ITE Certificate (*****Nitec*****)** for courses that cater to the upgrading needs of the workforce, and require completion of GCE ‘N’ Level or GCE ‘O’ Level as an entry requirement, with pre-requisites for certain courses.
- **Higher National ITE Certificate (*****Higher Nitec*****)** for courses that cater to the upgrading needs of the workforce, and require GCE ‘O’ Level or GCE 'N' (Academic) Level with pre-requisites as an entry requirement.
- **ITE Skills Certificate (ISC)**for courses that cater to the upgrading needs of the workforce.
- **SkillsFuture Series Certificate of Competency (COC)**for short courses that provide industry-relevant training in emerging and critical skills areas, comprising beginner to intermediate to advance levels.
- **Train The Trainer programme (TTT)**prepares trainers and On-the-Job Training practitioners to effectively instruct, coach, assess, and develop curriculum and assessments for industry training.

# Academic progression from full-time Higher Nitec

ITE training has become a practical and viable alternative route to tertiary education. At every course level, ITE has created opportunities for graduates to progress to higher level training both internally and externally.

Last updated 19 June 2026

Higher Nitec graduates with the following minimum GPA score (including CCA bonus points) may apply for admission to ITE Technical Diploma courses:

## Progression to Work-Study Diploma courses

The application period for 2026 intake is in **Nov 2025 to Feb 2026**.  [Click here for details on entry requirements and application](/current-full-time-students/progression/work-study-diploma/admission-for-work-study-diploma/) .

## Progression to Polytechnic Diploma courses

Higher Nitec graduates with a relevant GPA can also apply for admission to the first year of a related diploma course at the polytechnics. For some diploma courses in the Engineering / IT field, Higher Nitec graduates with a GPA ≥ 3.5 may be admitted directly to the second year of training. Please refer to  [JPAE website](https://jpae.polytechnic.edu.sg/app)  for more information on progression to diploma courses.

## National Service deferment and disruption policies

NS-liable males will be granted NS deferment for the pursuit of full-time studies at pre-university government-funded institutions including ITE if they attain a place and are pursuing a course for higher academic qualifications from what they have previously attained (e.g. from N/O Levels to Higher Nitec, from Nitec to Higher Nitec or from Nitec/ Higher Nitec to ITE Work-Study Diploma/Technical Engineer Diploma/Technical Diploma courses) and NS deferment will no longer be subject to cut-off ages.

For latest updates on NS deferment eligibility and policy, you can visit the  [https://for.edu.sg/ns-deferment](https://for.edu.sg/ns-deferment) . Students who are not eligible for NS deferment will need to withdraw from the course that they are enrolled in.

NS-enlisted males who plans to disrupt their NS for the pursuit of full-time studies at pre-university government-funded institutions including ITE can visit  [NS Disruption](https://www.ns.gov.sg/web/profiles/nsf/impt-full-time-ns-info#disruption-of-ftns)  page for more information.

# Academic progression from Nitec

ITE training has become a practical and viable alternative route to tertiary education. At every course level, ITE has created opportunities for graduates to progress to higher level training both internally and externally.

Last updated 19 June 2026

Nitec graduates with the following minimum GPA score (including CCA bonus points) may apply for admission to ITE Technical Diploma and Higher Nitec courses:

## Progression to Technical Diploma courses

Minimum GPA from relevant Nitec course (including CCA bonus points): **3.0**

- [Click here for details on entry requirements.](https://www.ite.edu.sg/current-full-time-students/progression/technical-diploma/application/)
- [Click here for the lists of related Technical Diploma courses for progression from a Nitec course](/current-full-time-students/progression/technical-diploma/) .
- [Click here for the application period](/current-full-time-students/progression/technical-diploma/application/)  for 2026 intake in **Nov 2025 to Feb 2026**.

## Progression to Work-Study Diploma courses

Minimum GPA from relevant Nitec course (including CCA bonus points): **2.0**

The application period for 2025 intake is in **Oct 2024 to Nov 2024**.  [Click here for details on entry requirements and application](/current-full-time-students/progression/work-study-diploma/admission-for-work-study-diploma/) .

## Progression to Higher Nitec courses

Minimum GPA from relevant Nitec courses for Progression to Higher Nitec courses

| Minimum GPA from relevant Nitec course (including CCA bonus points) | Required for |
| --- | --- |
| 3.0 | 2nd year of relatedHigher Niteccourses |
| 2.3 | 1st year ofHigher Niteccourses |
| 2.8 | 2nd year ofHigher Nitecin Automotive Engineering course1st year ofHigher NitecBusiness courses1st year ofHigher NitecHealth Sciences coursesHigher Nitecin Culinary Arts courseHigher Nitecin Early Childhood Education course*Higher Nitecin Hospitality Operations courseHigher Nitecin Pastry & Baking courseHigher Nitecin Precision Engineering course*Applicants for Higher Nitec in Early Childhood Education must also have obtained Grade 1 to 3 for GCE ‘N’ (Academic) English Language, OR Grade A1 to C6 for GCE ‘O’ Level English Language OR Grade A for GCE 'N' (Technical) English Language, OR and English Language Acceptable Alternative (ELAA) recognised by ECDA.Please click here for details [PDF, 16 KB]. |

The application period for 2026 intake is in **Jan 2026** (the exact application dates will be published on the ITE website following the release of 2025 GCE 'O' Level Examination results).  [Click here for details on application](/current-full-time-students/admissions/intake-exercise-for-ite-graduates/for-nitec-graduates/) .

## Progression to Polytechnic Diploma courses

Nitec (in technical areas) graduates with a GPA ≥ 3.5 may also apply for admission to a related diploma course at the polytechnics. Please refer to  [JPAE website](https://jpae.polytechnic.edu.sg/app)  for more information on progression to diploma courses.

## National Service deferment and disruption policies

NS-liable males will be granted NS deferment for the pursuit of full-time studies at pre-university government-funded institutions including ITE if they attain a place and are pursuing a course for higher academic qualifications from what they have previously attained (e.g. from N/O Levels to Higher Nitec, from Nitec to Higher Nitec or from Nitec/ Higher Nitec to ITE Work-Study Diploma/Technical Engineer Diploma/Technical Diploma courses) and NS deferment will no longer be subject to cut-off ages.

For latest updates on NS deferment eligibility and policy, please visit the  [https://for.edu.sg/ns-deferment](https://for.edu.sg/ns-deferment) . Students who are not eligible for NS deferment will need to withdraw from the course that they are enrolled in.

NS-enlisted males who plan to disrupt their NS for the pursuit of full-time studies at pre-university government-funded institutions including ITE can visit  [NS Disruption](https://www.ns.gov.sg/web/profiles/nsf/impt-full-time-ns-info#disruption-of-ftns)  page for more information.
